display_settings_saved: Toast after a display setting is saved, on the Displays page or in a device's display settings sheet.
nav_home: Sidebar and phone-bar entry; also the title of the first page, an overview of what is streaming and what needs attention.
nav_host: Sidebar entry, page title, and link in Home's attention card. The page about this host, the computer that streams: identity, settings, updates, power.
nav_displays: Sidebar and phone-menu entry and page title. The page for what happens to the host's screens while a device connects.
nav_devices: Sidebar and phone-bar entry, and link in Home's attention card. The page for pairing devices (clients such as phones, TVs, PCs) and listing paired ones.
nav_library: Sidebar and phone-bar entry for the page listing the host's games and where they come from.
nav_automation: Sidebar and phone-menu entry for the page of rules that run something when the host does something.
automation_title: Title of the Automation page, where the host's event hooks are managed.
automation_subtitle: Under the Automation page title. A hook is one command or webhook tied to one host event.
automation_hooks_title: Card title on the Automation page, above the list of hooks.
automation_add: Button in the 'Event hooks' card header; opens the hook dialog for a new hook.
automation_empty: Empty state of the 'Event hooks' card while no hook exists.
automation_edit: Screen-reader label of the pencil button on a hook row; opens that hook for editing.
automation_delete: Screen-reader label of the trash button on a hook row, and the red confirm button of 'Delete this hook?'.
automation_delete_confirm: Title of the confirm dialog opened by a hook row's trash button.
automation_unsaved: Bar under the hook list while edits are not yet sent to the host; next to the 'Discard changes' and 'Save' buttons.
automation_saved: Success toast after the hooks were saved to the host.
automation_save_failed: Error line in the 'Save automation?' password dialog when saving fails and the host gave no reason of its own.
automation_debounce_badge: Badge on a hook row. ms: whole milliseconds, the shortest time allowed between two runs of the hook, e.g. 500.
automation_elevated_badge: Badge on a hook row whose command runs with Windows administrator rights. Keep it short.
automation_field_elevated: Checkbox in the hook dialog, for commands only: the command runs with Windows administrator rights.
automation_field_elevated_help: Under the 'Run as administrator' checkbox. UAC is the Windows prompt that asks before a program gets administrator rights.
automation_field_elevated_off: Under the 'Run as administrator' checkbox while the host doesn't allow it. A shell command follows on the same line, so the text leads into it.
automation_hook_title: Title of the dialog that adds or edits one hook.
automation_hook_help: Subtitle of the hook dialog. A domain is the part of an event name before the dot, e.g. 'session' in session.*; '.*' is typed as is.
automation_hook_save: Confirm button of the hook dialog. It only puts the hook in the page's list; saving to the host is the page's 'Save' button.
automation_field_on: Label of the event dropdown in the hook dialog. Reads as a pair with 'Then' below it: when this happens, then do that.
automation_field_on_help: Under the event dropdown. The event names are identifiers such as session.started; they are not translated.
automation_field_action: Legend of the action choice in the hook dialog, and screen-reader label of its command or URL field. Pairs with 'When'.
automation_action_run: Toggle button in the hook dialog: the action is a shell command on the host. Sits beside 'Call a webhook'.
automation_action_webhook: Toggle button in the hook dialog: the action is an HTTP request to a URL. Sits beside 'Run a command'.
automation_action_run_help: Under the command field. stdin is standard input and PF_EVENT_* are environment variable names; both stay as written.
automation_action_webhook_help: Under the URL field when 'Call a webhook' is picked. POSTed means sent as an HTTP POST request.
automation_field_hmac: Label of a text field in the hook dialog, webhooks only. It takes a file path; HMAC is the request-signing method.
automation_field_hmac_help: Under the HMAC secret file field. The signature is sent with the webhook request.
automation_field_filter: Checkbox in the hook dialog; ticking it shows fields that limit the hook to one device, profile, game or settings preset.
automation_filter_client: Label of a dropdown of paired devices in the hook filter. The hook fires only for the chosen device.
automation_filter_profile: Label of a dropdown in the hook filter, shown when there are several profiles. A profile is one player's identity on this host.
automation_filter_app: Label of the game field in the hook filter. It takes a game id such as steam:570 and suggests games by title.
event_any_client: Option in the Hook dialog's 'When' list, beside the code client.*. Matches every client event (connect, disconnect).
event_any_session: Option in the Hook dialog's 'When' list, beside the code session.*. Matches every session event (start, end).
event_any_stream: Option in the Hook dialog's 'When' list, beside the code stream.*. Matches every stream event (start, stop).
event_any_game: Option in the Hook dialog's 'When' list, beside the code game.*. Matches every game event (launching, running, window, exit).
event_any_pairing: Option in the Hook dialog's 'When' list, beside the code pairing.*. Matches every pairing event (requested, completed, denied).
event_any_display: Option in the Hook dialog's 'When' list, beside the code display.*. Matches every virtual display event (created, released).
automation_filter_app_help: Under 'Game / app id'. steam:570 is a literal example id; 'the title' is the game's name shown beside the suggestions.
automation_filter_preset: Label of a text field in the hook filter. A settings preset is a named set of stream settings saved on a client device.
automation_filter_preset_help: Under 'Settings preset'. Docked is a sample preset name.
automation_filter_none: Shown in the 'Game / app id' list of the hook dialog when nothing matches the typed id; the id is saved as typed anyway.
automation_filter_any_device: First entry of the 'Client name' list in the hook dialog: the hook runs for whichever device triggers it.
automation_filter_any_profile: First entry of the 'Profile' list in the hook dialog: the hook runs for every profile.
automation_field_debounce: Label of a number field in the hook dialog: the shortest gap, in milliseconds, between two runs of the hook.
automation_field_timeout: Label of a number field in the hook dialog: seconds, 1 to 600, before the host gives up on the hook.
automation_field_hold: Checkbox in the hook dialog, only for the game-launching event: the game's start waits until the hook finishes.
automation_field_hold_help: Under the 'Hold the launch' checkbox. 'timeout' and 'minimum gap' are the fields 'Timeout (s)' and 'Minimum gap (ms)'.
automation_confirm_title: Title of the console-password dialog opened by 'Save' on the Automation page.
automation_confirm_body: Body of the 'Save automation?' dialog. The console password is the one for signing in to this web console.
library_delete_failed: Toast when deleting a custom game fails and the host gave no reason.
library_hide_failed: Toast when hiding or showing a title fails and the host gave no reason.
gpu_apply_failed: Toast on the Host page when saving the GPU choice fails and the host gave no reason.
stats_start_failed: Error toast when 'Start capture' fails and the host gave no reason. Performance page under Diagnostics.
stats_stop_failed: Error toast when 'Stop & save' fails and the host gave no reason. The recording may be lost, which the text says.
stats_delete_failed: Error toast when deleting a saved recording fails and the host gave no reason.
stats_download_failed: Error toast when downloading a saved recording fails and the host gave no reason.
games_end_failed: Toast on Home when ending a running game fails and the host gave no reason.
action_stop_failed: Error toast on the Home page when stopping a session fails and the host gave no reason.
action_idr_failed: Error toast on the Home page when the keyframe request fails and the host gave no reason.
nav_settings: Sidebar and phone-menu entry for the console's own settings: language, sidebar, appearance, sign out.
nav_close_menu: Screen-reader label of the invisible backdrop that closes the phone's 'More' menu when tapped.
nav_more: Last tab in the phone's bottom bar; opens a menu with the remaining pages. Very narrow, keep it short.
common_details: Label of a collapsed section that unfolds more facts; used on a session row on Home and on the Host page's card.
common_more_actions: Tooltip and screen-reader label of a '…' menu button on a row or toolbar; the menu holds the less common actions.
nav_plugins: Sidebar and phone-menu entry for the page to add and manage plugins; also the heading above the unpinned plugins in the phone menu.
plugin_offline_title: Heading of a card on a plugin's page when the plugin's backend doesn't answer. The plugin's name and the retry hint follow.
plugin_origin_untrusted_title: Heading of a card on a plugin's page when the browser doesn't yet accept the host's certificate for the plugin's separate port.
plugin_origin_untrusted_hint: Under 'Trust this plugin's port once'; a docs link follows. The certificate is the host's own; opening the address once in a tab fixes it.
plugin_origin_untrusted_open: Button under 'Trust this plugin's port once'; opens the plugin's address in a new browser tab.
plugin_origin_unavailable_title: Heading of a card on a plugin's page when the host's plugin-page port didn't start, so no plugin pages can be shown.
plugin_origin_unavailable_hint: Under 'Plugin interfaces are unavailable'; a docs link follows. PUNKTFUNK_UI_PLUGIN_PORT is an environment variable name; keep it as is.
plugin_offline_hint: After the plugin's name and a dash, under 'This plugin isn't running'. The scripting runner is the 'Plugin runner' service; shell commands follow.
plugin_retry: Button on the cards 'This plugin isn't running' and 'Trust this plugin's port once'; checks again whether the plugin is reachable.
plugin_open_new_tab: Link at the top of a plugin's page that opens the plugin full-window in a new browser tab. Also its tooltip and screen-reader label.
home_now: Card title on Home above the sessions and games streaming at this moment.
home_now_empty: Empty state inside the 'Now' card on Home.
home_recent_sessions: Card title on Home above a list of the last few finished sessions.
home_attention_pending: Line in Home's attention card, followed by a link to the Devices page. names: the waiting devices' names, comma-separated.
home_attention_audio: Line in Home's attention card, followed by a link to the Host page. state: a short status such as 'Not wired' or 'No game audio'.
home_own_desktop: Detail on a Home row for a profile that plays on its own desktop session (a seat) instead of the host's screen.
status_last_copy: Button in a finished session's details on Home; copies the session's raw data to the clipboard so it can be pasted into a bug report.
status_last_copied: The same button as 'Copy for a bug report', for a moment after the copy worked.
status_last_bitrate: One fact in a finished session's details line, between middle dots. mbit: the bitrate as a number such as 24.5.
status_last_bitrate_avg: Same fact when the bitrate varied during the session. mbit: the average as a number such as 24.5.
status_last_steps: One fact in a finished session's details line. count: how many times the automatic bitrate changed during the session.
status_last_audio_late: One fact in a finished session's details line. count: audio frames that arrived too late to be played.
status_last_gyro: One fact in a finished session's details line. count: times the client's motion-sensor (gyro) data stopped arriving.
status_last_dropped: One fact in a finished session's details line. count: video frames lost on the way to the client.
status_last_join: One fact in a finished session's details line: it used a display that another session already had. A fragment, no final period.
status_last_ended: Last fact in a finished session's details line. reason: one of the 'the client stopped it' style fragments.
status_last_end_local: A reason after 'ended:' in a finished session's details; a fragment, not a sentence. The client device ended the session.
status_last_end_game_exited: A reason after 'ended:' in a finished session's details; a fragment, not a sentence. The game quit.
status_last_end_host_ended: A reason after 'ended:' in a finished session's details; a fragment, not a sentence. The host closed the session normally.
status_last_end_host_error: A reason after 'ended:' in a finished session's details; a fragment, not a sentence. The host stopped on an internal error.
status_last_end_lost: A reason after 'ended:' in a finished session's details; a fragment, not a sentence. The network link to the client dropped.
status_last_end_stopped: A reason after 'ended:' in a finished session's details; a fragment, not a sentence. The person using this console pressed Stop.
status_last_end_stolen: A reason after 'ended:' in a finished session's details; a fragment, not a sentence. A second device took over the display.
audio_wiring_title: Label in the Host page's details for how the host's game audio and microphone are set up; a status badge follows it.
audio_output: Label before a device name, in the same line as 'Microphone'. The sound the game makes, which the host captures and streams to the client.
audio_microphone: Label before a device name, in the same line as 'Game audio'. The microphone endpoint on the host.
audio_unavailable: Value after the 'Game audio' or 'Microphone' label when the host has no such device.
audio_ready: Green badge next to 'Audio wiring': game audio and microphone both work.
audio_ready_no_mic: Gray badge next to 'Audio wiring': game audio works and there is no microphone.
audio_no_output: Red badge next to 'Audio wiring', and the state in Home's attention line: a microphone exists but no game audio.
audio_none: Red badge next to 'Audio wiring', and the state in Home's attention line: neither game audio nor microphone is set up.
audio_mic_withheld: Note under the audio line on the Host page. Steam is the game store; the host can create its own virtual microphone once it is installed.
audio_last_resort: Note under the audio line on the Host page: game audio is on a fallback device.
stream_codec: Label of a row in a live session's details on Home; the value is the video codec, such as HEVC.
stream_resolution: Label of a row in a live session's details on Home; the value is width × height in pixels.
stream_fps: Label of a row in a live session's details on Home; the value is frames per second.
stream_first_frame: Label of a row in a live session's details on Home; the value is the milliseconds from connecting to the first picture.
stream_last_resize: Label of a row in a live session's details on Home; the value is the milliseconds the last resolution change took.
stream_capture_health: Label of a row in a live session's details on Home; the value is the state of the host's screen capture.
stream_last_recovery: Label of a row in a live session's details on Home; the value says how the last capture stall was repaired.
stream_packet_size: Label of a row in a live session's details on Home; the value is bytes per video packet.
stream_min_fec: Label of a row in a live session's details on Home; the value is the fewest error-correction (FEC) packets per block that the client asks for.
stream_bitrate: Label of a row in a live session's details on Home; the value is the video data rate in Mbit/s.
activity_title: Card title on the Home page, above the list of the host's latest events.
activity_empty: Empty state of the 'Recent activity' card on the Home page.
activity_show_all: Button at the bottom of the 'Recent activity' card; expands the short list to every entry.
activity_ring_note: Footnote in the 'Recent activity' card, shown only after 'Show all'. The list lives in the browser and is lost on reload.
activity_client_connected: Event label (activity row badge, Hook 'When' list): a client device connected to the host. The device name follows in the row.
activity_client_disconnected: Event label (activity row badge, Hook 'When' list): a client device is no longer connected.
activity_session_started: Event label (activity row badge, Hook 'When' list): a streaming session opened for a client.
activity_session_ended: Event label (activity row badge, Hook 'When' list): a streaming session closed.
activity_stream_started: Event label (activity row badge, Hook 'When' list): the video and audio stream began flowing.
activity_stream_stopped: Event label (activity row badge, Hook 'When' list): the video and audio stream stopped.
activity_game_launching: Event label (activity row badge, Hook 'When' list): the host is about to start a game for a client. A state, earlier than 'Game running'.
activity_game_running: Event label (activity row badge, Hook 'When' list): the game's process is up, but its window may not be on screen yet.
activity_game_window: Event label (activity row badge, Hook 'When' list): the game's own window has reached the screen.
activity_game_exited: Event label (activity row badge, Hook 'When' list): the game ended, whether the player quit or the host closed it.
activity_pairing_pending: Event label (activity row badge, Hook 'When' list): a device asked to pair and waits for approval.
activity_pairing_completed: Event label (activity row badge, Hook 'When' list): a device finished pairing. Short, past tense; shown in green.
activity_pairing_denied: Event label (activity row badge, Hook 'When' list): a pairing request was refused. Shown in red.
activity_access_granted: Event label (activity row badge, Hook 'When' list): an operator gave a device an access level, such as full or view only.
activity_access_changed: Event label (activity row badge, Hook 'When' list): a paired device's access level or time limit was edited afterwards.
activity_access_expired: Event label (activity row badge, Hook 'When' list): a device's time-limited access ran out while it was in a session.
activity_display_created: Event label (activity row badge, Hook 'When' list): the host created a virtual display for a stream.
activity_display_released: Event label (activity row badge, Hook 'When' list): kept virtual displays were removed.
activity_library_changed: Event label (activity row badge, Hook 'When' list): the game library's contents changed.
activity_emulators_changed: Event label (activity row badge, Hook 'When' list): a managed emulator was installed or removed.
activity_downloads_changed: Event label (activity row badge, Hook 'When' list): a game download changed state or its files were removed.
activity_update_available: Event label (activity row badge, Hook 'When' list): a newer Punktfunk version was found for this host.
activity_update_applied: Event label (activity row badge, Hook 'When' list): a software update finished installing on the host.
activity_plugins_changed: Event label (activity row badge, Hook 'When' list): a plugin registered, restarted or went away.
activity_store_changed: Event label (activity row badge, Hook 'When' list): the plugin and emulator store's catalog or installed items changed.
activity_settings_changed: Event label (activity row badge, Hook 'When' list): an operator changed the host's settings.
activity_action_invoked: Event label (activity row badge, Hook 'When' list): a host action such as restart or sleep was requested.
activity_host_started: Event label (activity row badge, Hook 'When' list): the host program came up. Shown in green.
activity_host_stopping: Event label (activity row badge, Hook 'When' list): the host program is shutting down.
action_stop_session: Red button on a live session row on the Home page; ends that session.
action_request_idr: Button or menu item on a Home session row. Asks the video encoder for a complete fresh picture, which clears a garbled image.
action_unpair: Verb. Button in the 'Edit access' sheet, tooltip and screen-reader label of the trash button on a paired device, and confirm button of 'Unpair this device?'.
action_unpair_all: Menu item in the Devices page's more-actions menu, and confirm button of its dialog; removes every pairing.
action_rename: Verb. Confirm button of the rename prompts, and tooltip and screen-reader label of the pencil button on a profile row and the device name.
connect_help: Hint under the two copy fields at the top of the Host page ('Host address' and 'Deep link').
connect_address: Label over the host's IP address, in a copy field at the top of the Host page.
connect_link: Label over a copy field holding a punktfunk:// link that opens a client straight onto this host.
connect_copy: aria-label (screen-reader only) of the icon button that copies the field's value.
host_up_to_date: Status in the Host page's header line, next to the version: the host runs the newest release.
host_updating: Status in the Host page's header line while a software update installs.
host_check_update: Button in the Host page's header that looks for a new Punktfunk release.
host_power_menu: Tooltip and aria-label of the ⋯ button that opens the host's power actions (sleep, restart, shut down).
host_hostname: Fact name under 'Details' on the Host page; the value is the machine's network name.
host_os: Fact name under 'Details' on the Host page; the value is an OS name with a short id in parentheses.
host_local_ip: Fact name under 'Details' on the Host page; the value is the host's address on the local network.
host_version: Fact name under 'Details' on the Host page; the value is the Punktfunk version the host runs.
host_gamestream_version: Fact name under 'Details' on the Host page, shown only with GameStream on; the version number reported to Moonlight clients.
host_abi: Fact name under 'Details' on the Host page; the value is a plain number, the version of the host's client interface.
host_codecs: Fact name under 'Details' on the Host page; the values are video codec badges such as HEVC and AV1.
host_ports: Fact name under 'Details' on the Host page; the values are badges of the network ports the host listens on.
host_uniqueid: Fact name under 'Details' on the Host page; the value is the host's permanent identifier string.
host_power_confirm_body: Body of the confirm dialog for a host power action (sleep, restart, shut down); asks for the web console password.
host_power_sent: Toast after the host accepted a power action. action: the action's name, such as Restart or Shut down.
host_power_working: Label of the confirm button while a power action is being sent.
host_compositors: Fact name under 'Details' on the Host page (Linux hosts); the values are badges of the display servers (compositors) the host can use.
compositor_unavailable: Added to a compositor badge on the Host page, after a middle dot: this display backend can't be used on this host.
compositor_default: Added to a compositor badge on the Host page, after a middle dot: the host uses this display backend unless told otherwise.
host_gpus: Label of the graphics card row in the Host page's video settings; also the aria-label of its dropdown.
host_gpus_help: Hint under the 'GPUs' row. 'Automatic' is the first option of the dropdown beside it.
gpu_automatic: Option in the GPU drop-down on the Host page: the host picks the graphics card. The current pick's name may follow.
gpu_in_use: Green badge beside the GPU row's title: the card encoding right now. backend: the encoder in capitals, such as NVENC or VAAPI.
gpu_missing_warning: Amber warning under the GPU row. name: the name of the graphics card the operator chose earlier.
gpu_env_note: Note under the GPU row. The capitals are an environment variable on the host. value: the id it is set to.
gpu_encoder_pin_note: Note under the GPU row. The capitals are an environment variable on the host. value: the encoder backend it names, such as nvenc.
gpu_encoder_pin_warning: Amber warning under the GPU row. value: the pinned encoder; vendor: the card maker, such as NVIDIA; name: the card the next session uses; host.env is a file.
host_conflicts_title: Heading of a warning card on the Host page, shown only on a conflict; the other programs' names are listed below it.
host_conflicts_help: Body of the warning card 'Another game-streaming server is active…'. 'Restart' means restarting Punktfunk.
display_preset_default: Name of a built-in preset card under 'When a device connects' on the Displays page: the safe baseline.
display_preset_gaming_rig: Name of a preset card on the Displays page, for a host with no monitor attached. Short, sits on one line.
display_preset_shared_desktop: Name of a preset card on the Displays page, for a host that is also used in person.
display_preset_hotdesk: Name of a preset card on the Displays page: one person at a time, moving between their devices.
display_preset_workstation: Name of a preset card on the Displays page, for a host used daily with several monitors.
display_preset_play_together: Name of a preset card on the Displays page: friends connect and all see and use the same screen.
display_keep_alive_seconds: Unit beside a number field, and that field's screen-reader label: a duration in seconds. Used in Customise and Host settings.
display_release_all: Menu item at the top of the Displays page. Removes every virtual screen kept after its device disconnected.
display_game_session: Question label in Customise on the Displays page: whether a game opens in its own session. Options: 'Auto', 'Dedicated'.
display_game_session_help: Hint under 'Dedicated game sessions'. 'Dedicated' is one of its two options.
display_game_session_auto: Option under 'Dedicated game sessions': the host decides how a game starts.
display_game_session_dedicated: Option under 'Dedicated game sessions': a game starts in a separate session at the device's resolution.
display_ddc: Label of an on/off switch under 'Advanced' on the Displays page. DDC/CI is the monitor power-control protocol; keep the acronym.
display_ddc_help: Hint under 'Power monitors off (DDC/CI)', followed by a Docs link. Says what the switch fixes.
display_pnp: Label of an on/off switch under 'Advanced' on the Displays page. PnP is Windows Plug and Play; keep the acronym.
display_pnp_help: Hint under 'Disable monitor devices (PnP)', followed by a Docs link. Says what the switch prevents.
display_edid: Label of an on/off switch under 'Advanced' on the Displays page. EDID is the identity data a monitor reports; keep the acronym.
display_edid_help: Hint under 'Hold monitor identity (EDID)', followed by a Docs link.
display_preset_save_as: Button under the preset cards on the Displays page. Opens a name prompt to store the current settings as a custom preset.
display_preset_save_title: Title of the name prompt opened by 'Save as preset…'.
display_preset_name: Field label in the prompt for saving or renaming a custom preset. The value is the preset's name.
display_preset_edit: Icon-button tooltip on a custom preset card, and the title of the prompt it opens. Renames the preset.
display_preset_update: Icon-button tooltip on a custom preset card. Overwrites the preset with the display settings in force now.
display_preset_delete: Icon-button tooltip on a custom preset card, and the confirm button of 'Delete this custom preset?'.
display_preset_delete_confirm: Title of the confirm dialog before deleting a custom preset, a set of display settings the user saved.
clients_rename_title: Title of the rename dialog opened from a paired Moonlight device's name.
clients_rename_body: Body of the rename dialog for a paired Moonlight device, above the name field. 'It' is the display name.
clients_rename_label: Label of an optional device-name field: in the rename dialog and in the Moonlight step of the pairing sheet.
clients_rename_failed: Toast when renaming a Moonlight device failed.
pairing_title: Page title of the Devices page.
pairing_idle: Moonlight step of the 'Pair a device' sheet while no Moonlight client is waiting; the PIN comes from the Moonlight app.
pairing_waiting: Moonlight step of the 'Pair a device' sheet, above the PIN field it introduces.
pairing_ceremony_device: Names a waiting Moonlight client, also each picker option. uniqueid: its ID; ip: its address; fp: last 10 characters of its certificate fingerprint.
pairing_ceremony_select: Moonlight step of the 'Pair a device' sheet when several clients wait; also the picker's placeholder.
pairing_pin_label: Label of the PIN field in the Moonlight step; the digits are shown by the Moonlight app.
pairing_submit: Button in the Moonlight step that sends the entered PIN to the waiting client.
pairing_pin_sent: Note under the Moonlight step's button once the PIN was handed over. 'Paired devices' is a group heading on the Devices page.
pairing_failed: Inline error in the Moonlight step after sending the PIN failed.
pairing_native_title: Title of the 'Pair a device' sheet and label of the Devices page button that opens it.
pairing_sheet_moonlight: Text button at the foot of the 'Pair a device' sheet, shown with GameStream on; switches to the Moonlight PIN step.
devices_armed: Row in the Devices page's waiting list while a PIN is shown. pin: the PIN digits; time: a countdown such as 1:45.
devices_moonlight_waiting: Row in the Devices page's waiting list while a Moonlight client waits for its PIN.
devices_moonlight_enter: Button on that row; opens the Moonlight PIN step. Keep it short.
devices_will_play_as: Part of a waiting device's detail line, after its age. name: the profile name the device asks to play as.
devices_streaming: Green badge on a paired device's row while that device is streaming.
pairing_native_desc: Intro in the 'Pair a device' sheet before a PIN exists. A one-time PIN stops working after one pairing attempt, right or wrong.
pairing_native_disabled: Message in the 'Pair a device' sheet when the host runs without the Punktfunk protocol. The backticked command stays as typed.
pairing_native_arm: Button in the 'Pair a device' sheet that creates and shows the PIN, after the console password is typed.
pairing_native_bound_for: Heading when the PIN was made for one device; also detail in the waiting row. name: the device's name.
pairing_native_bound_hint: Pair device sheet, under 'PIN for {name}' when the PIN was made for one device. A PIN works for a single pairing attempt; other devices' attempts are refused without using it up.
pairing_native_bound_clear: Button beside 'PIN for {name}'; drops the restriction to one device so any device can use the PIN.
pairing_native_enter: Line above the large PIN digits in the 'Pair a device' sheet; the PIN goes into the Punktfunk app on the device.
pairing_native_expires: Label before a countdown such as 1:45 under the PIN; the PIN stops working at zero.
pairing_native_cancel: Button that withdraws the shown PIN, in the sheet and in the waiting row. It cancels nothing else.
pairing_native_devices: Heading above the list of paired devices on the Devices page.
devices_col_device: Column header of the paired devices list on the Devices page; the column holds name and protocol.
devices_col_access: Column header of the paired devices list; on a phone a small label over the value. The column shows what the device may do.
devices_col_display: Column header of the paired devices list; on a phone a small label over the value. The column shows the device's display setup.
pairing_native_empty: Empty state of the paired devices list.
pairing_native_unpair_confirm: Title of the confirm dialog for unpairing one device.
pairing_native_unpair_body: Body of the confirm dialog for unpairing one device.
pairing_native_unpair_all_confirm: Title of the confirm dialog for unpairing every device. count: number of paired devices.
pairing_native_unpair_all_body: Body of the unpair-all dialog. 'punktfunk/2' and 'Moonlight' are the two kinds of paired device.
pairing_knock_title: Toast title shown anywhere in the console when a device asks to pair. Its action button opens the Devices page.
pairing_knock_desc: Toast text under 'A device wants to pair'. name: the device's name.
pairing_knock_action: Button in that toast; opens the Devices page to decide.
pairing_native_unpair_all_failed: Toast when unpairing all devices failed in part or whole.
pairing_native_unpair_failed: Toast when unpairing one device failed. name: the device's name.
pairing_protocol_native: Protocol label on a paired device's line; the name of the Punktfunk protocol, not a sentence.
pairing_protocol_moonlight: Protocol label on a paired device's line, before its fingerprint; a device paired through the Moonlight app.
pairing_pending_title: Group heading on the Devices page above devices that asked to pair and wait for a decision.
pairing_pending_approve: Button that accepts a waiting device, on its row and in the approve dialog.
pairing_pending_deny: Icon-only button on a waiting device's row (aria-label and tooltip); refuses the request.
pairing_pending_from_internet: Badge on a waiting device's row: the request came over the internet, not the local network.
pairing_pending_arm: Button on a waiting device's row where Approve is not offered; shows a PIN made for that device.
pairing_pending_wan_hint: Tooltip of 'Arm PIN' for a request from the internet. A device chooses its own name, so the name is not trusted.
pairing_pending_through_web_client: Badge on a waiting device's row: the request came through the Punktfunk web client.
pairing_pending_relayed_hint: Tooltip of 'Arm PIN' for a request that came through the web client.
pairing_pending_from_new_page: Badge on a waiting device's row: the request came from a web page this host has not seen before.
pairing_pending_new_page_hint: Tooltip of 'Arm PIN' for a request from a page new to this host.
pairing_pending_name_prompt: Label of the device-name field in the approve dialog; placeholder of the optional name field in the Moonlight step.
pairing_pending_name_title: Title of the dialog for approving a waiting device.
pairing_pending_name_desc: First sentence of the approve dialog's description, followed by 'Choose what this device may do…'. name: the device's name; fp: start of its fingerprint.
pairing_pending_age_just_now: How long ago a pairing request arrived, in a waiting device's detail line: under ten seconds.
pairing_pending_age_secs: Age of a pairing request in the detail line, joined with · to other parts. s: whole seconds, 10 to 59.
pairing_pending_age_mins: Age of a pairing request in the detail line. min: whole minutes, 1 or more.
pairing_approve_desc: Second sentence of the approve dialog's description; the controls below are access level and expiry.
pairing_approve_known_note: Note in the approve dialog when the device was paired before.
pairing_approve_guest: Button in the approve dialog that approves in one click with 'Controller only' for 4 hours.
pairing_approve_guest_hint: Beside 'Approve as guest'. 'Controller only' is an access level; the 4 hours match 'In 4 hours'.
pairing_password_help: Hint under the console password field in the 'Pair a device' sheet, the approve dialog and the Moonlight step.
access_level_label: Label of the access level dropdown in the pair, approve and edit dialogs; also a menu label on a streaming session's row on Home.
access_level_full: Access level option: the device may do everything. Also in Home's session menu.
access_level_controller: Access level option: the device may send game controller input only. Also in Home's session menu.
access_level_view: Access level option: the device may watch but send no input. Also in Home's session menu.
access_level_custom: Access level shown when the individual toggles match no preset; a state the user never picks.
access_advanced: Toggle under the access level dropdown that shows the individual permission checkboxes.
access_grant_gamepad: Checkbox under 'Advanced': the device may send game controller input.
access_grant_pointer: Checkbox under 'Advanced': the device may send mouse, touch and pen input.
access_grant_keyboard: Checkbox under 'Advanced': the device may send keyboard input.
access_grant_clipboard: Checkbox under 'Advanced': the device may share its clipboard with the host.
access_grant_mic: Checkbox under 'Advanced': the device may send its microphone to the host.
access_grant_launch: Checkbox under 'Advanced': the device may start games on the host.
access_grant_power: Checkbox under 'Advanced': the device may sleep, restart or shut down the host.
access_grant_power_caption: Line under the 'Host power' checkbox. Host: the computer Punktfunk runs on.
access_grant_manage_games: Checkbox under 'Advanced': the device may pause game downloads and remove games from the host.
access_grant_manage_games_caption: Line under 'Manage games'. 'Launch games' is another checkbox in the same list.
access_expires_label: Label of the expiry dropdown in the pair, approve and edit dialogs.
access_expires_keep: Dropdown option under 'Access expires', edit dialog only: the device's current deadline stays.
access_expires_forever: Dropdown option under 'Access expires': access never ends.
access_expires_1h: Dropdown option under 'Access expires': access ends after one hour.
access_expires_4h: Dropdown option under 'Access expires': access ends after four hours.
access_expires_8h: Dropdown option under 'Access expires': access ends after eight hours.
access_expires_session: Dropdown option under 'Access expires': access ends when the device's session ends. 'They' is the person using the device.
access_until_disconnect: Chip suffix after ·, e.g. 'Controller only · until they disconnect'; same meaning as 'Until they disconnect'.
access_expires_custom: Dropdown option under 'Access expires'; opens an hours field, hence the ellipsis.
access_expires_custom_hours: Label of the number field (1 to 720) shown after picking 'Custom…'.
access_left_days: Chip suffix after ·, e.g. 'Controller only · 3 d left'. d: whole days, 2 or more. Short: the chip never wraps.
access_left_hours: Chip suffix after ·. h: whole hours, 1 to 47. Short: the chip never wraps.
access_left_minutes: Chip suffix after ·. min: whole minutes, 1 to 60. Short: the chip never wraps.
access_left_under_minute: Chip suffix after ·, for the last minute of access. Short: the chip never wraps.
access_expired: Warning badge that replaces the access chip once a device's access has run out.
access_ungoverned: Badge in the Access column for Moonlight devices, which have full control because access levels do not apply to them.
access_edit_title: Title of the edit access dialog and of the password dialog for widening access; also tooltip of the access chip.
access_edit_desc: Description in the edit access dialog. name: the device's name, or the start of its fingerprint if unnamed.
access_expire_now: Button in the edit access dialog; ends the device's access at once and cuts its live sessions.
access_edit_failed: Toast and dialog error after saving a device's access failed; also from Home's session menu.
access_widen_confirm_body: Body of the password dialog shown when an access change gives a device more rights or a later deadline.
pairing_moonlight_title: Title of the 'Pair a device' sheet on its Moonlight step. Moonlight is a third-party client; GameStream is its protocol.
library_title: Page title of the game library, and the link back to it at the top of a game's page.
library_empty: Library page empty state, first line, when the host lists no games. Followed by 'Add a game source under Sources…'.
library_sources_title: Section heading on the Library page's Sources tab: the stores and launchers that supply games.
library_sources_help: Hint under the game sources list. 'One' is a source, switched with its checkbox.
library_sources_failed: Toast when switching a game source on or off fails.
library_store_steam: Store name on a game's badge and in its page header. A brand name.
library_store_custom: Badge on a game the operator added by hand, not synced from a source.
library_add_title: Heading of the new-game page until a title is typed; the game is added by hand.
library_process_legend: Card title on a game's Launch tab; the fields in it are optional hints.
library_process_help: Hint under 'Process (optional)'. The host watches the game's process to see it exit or to end it on disconnect.
library_field_exe: Field label on the Launch tab under 'Process (optional)'. A file path on the host.
library_field_exe_help: Hint under 'Executable path'. The path is a literal example.
library_field_install_dir: Field label on the Launch tab under 'Process (optional)'. A folder on the host.
library_field_install_dir_help: Hint under 'Install directory'. Wine and Proton run Windows games on Linux.
library_field_process_name: Field label on the Launch tab under 'Process (optional)'. The program's name as the OS lists it.
library_field_process_name_help: Hint under 'Process name'. 'eden' is a literal example, an emulator's program name.
library_add_button: Button in the Library page header; opens the new-game page to add a custom game by hand.
library_field_title: Field label on a game's Information tab: the game's name.
library_field_command: Field label on the Launch tab: a shell command the host runs to start the game.
library_field_password_help: Hint under the console password field in a game's header, shown when the save carries a command. 'As you' means the host's user account.
library_field_platform: Field label on the Information tab: the system a game runs on, such as a console or PC.
library_field_platform_help: Hint under 'Platform'. The system names are literal examples.
library_field_description: Field label on the Information tab: the game's description, a multi-line text box.
library_field_developer: Field label on the Information tab: the studio that made the game.
library_field_publisher: Field label on the Information tab: the company that published the game.
library_field_release_year: Field label on the Information tab: a year, numeric input.
library_field_genres: Field label on the Information tab: a comma-separated list of genres.
library_field_genres_help: Hint under 'Genres'. Entries are split at ASCII commas; the examples are literal.
library_field_tags: Field label on the Information tab: the operator's own labels for organizing games.
library_field_tags_help: Hint under 'Tags'. Entries are split at ASCII commas; the examples are literal.
library_field_region: Field label on the Information tab: the release region of a console game.
library_field_region_help: Hint under 'Region'. NTSC-U, PAL and NTSC-J are literal region codes.
library_field_players: Field label on the Information tab: how many players the game supports, numeric input.
library_provider_count: Source row on the Sources tab, after its status: how many games it synced. count: number of entries.
library_launchers_title: Caption before the chips above the games. A launcher is an entry that opens a store app such as Steam, not a game.
library_empty_add_source: Library page empty state, second line. 'Sources' is the tab of that name, next to 'Games'.
library_add_source: Heading above the install buttons under a source list on the Sources tab; shown for game sources and Art & Metadata.
library_metadata_title: Section heading on the Sources tab, and a category in the Store. These sources supply cover art and descriptions.
library_metadata_help: Hint under the Art & Metadata list, which is ordered top to bottom. 'Use for every game' is an option in a row's menu.
library_metadata_replace: Checkbox in an Art & Metadata row's ⋯ menu: this source may overwrite cover art a game already has.
library_metadata_replace_help: Tooltip on 'Use for every game' in the row's menu.
library_metadata_up: Icon button on an Art & Metadata row (tooltip and screen-reader label): ranks the source higher.
library_metadata_down: Icon button on an Art & Metadata row (tooltip and screen-reader label): ranks the source lower.
library_metadata_found: Status in an Art & Metadata row. found: games it has art or details for; wanted: games worth looking up (they lack some).
library_metadata_failed: Toast when saving the Art & Metadata order or switches fails and the host gave no reason.
library_metadata_silent: Row text for an installed Art & Metadata source that reported nothing yet. 'Logs' is the Logs page.
library_media_from: Caption under an artwork preview on the Media tab: which source supplied the image. source: the source's name.
library_media_picked: Caption under an artwork preview when the operator chose the image through 'Choose…'.
library_media_choose: Button under an artwork preview; opens a dialog to pick another image.
library_media_reset: Button under an artwork preview; drops the hand-picked image and returns to what the sources provide.
library_media_choose_title: Title of the image-picking dialog. slot: the artwork slot's name, such as 'Portrait' or 'Logo'.
library_media_no_sources: Image-picking dialog text when no Art & Metadata source is running. 'Library' is the Library page.
library_media_matched: In the image-picking dialog beside a source's name: the game it matched. label: that game's name in the source.
library_media_no_match: In the image-picking dialog beside a source's name: the source found no game for this title.
library_media_change_match: Button in the image-picking dialog, a question; opens a search for another game in the source.
library_media_unpin: Button in the image-picking dialog; drops the hand-picked match and returns to the source's own.
library_media_search: Button that runs the match search in the image-picking dialog, and the screen-reader label of its field.
library_media_no_results: Image-picking dialog text when the match search finds nothing.
library_media_no_images: Image-picking dialog text under a source that has no image for the chosen artwork slot.
library_media_paste: Label of the web-address field at the bottom of the image-picking dialog.
library_media_use: Button beside 'Or paste an image URL'; uses the pasted address as the image.
library_media_pick_failed: Toast when saving a picked image fails and the host gave no reason.
library_media_source_failed: Toast or error in the image-picking dialog. source: the source's name; issue: the error text, often English.
library_field_from: Suffix after a field label on a read-only game's Information tab, e.g. 'Developer · from …'. source: the source's name.
library_field_from_editable: Hint under an Information field on an editable game whose value a source filled in. source: the source's name.
library_source_detected: Badge on the install button of a launcher the host found installed.
library_source_running: Status in a source row, before the entry count: its plugin is running. A state, not an action.
library_source_stopped: Status in a source row, before the entry count: its plugin is not running. A state.
library_source_access_pending: Link under a source row that opens its folder requests. title: the source's name; count: folders awaiting a decision.
library_source_absent: Detail line in a source row when the host looked for that launcher and found none. title: the source's name.
plugin_access_folders: Toggle under an installed plugin (Installed tab) that lists the folders it was allowed or refused. count: number of those folders.
plugin_access_read_only: Label beside a folder path in a plugin's access list: the plugin can read the folder but not change it.
plugin_access_read_files: Label beside a folder path: the plugin can read the files directly in this folder, not those in subfolders.
plugin_access_read_write: Label beside a folder path: the plugin can read and change the folder's contents.
plugin_access_allow: Button on a plugin's folder request that grants it. Also the confirm button of the 'Allow access?' dialog.
plugin_access_allowing: Label of the confirm button in the 'Allow access?' dialog while the request runs.
plugin_access_walk: Progress line under a folder while its access is being granted; a large Windows folder takes minutes. seconds: whole seconds so far.
plugin_access_walk_back: Progress line under a folder while its access is being withdrawn; a large Windows folder takes minutes. seconds: whole seconds so far.
plugin_access_prompt_title: Title of a dialog that opens on any page when a plugin requests a folder. plugin: the plugin's name.
plugin_access_prompt_body: Body of that dialog. 'Later' is its button; 'Library' and 'Sources' are the page and its tab where the request stays.
plugin_access_later: Button that closes the folder request dialog and keeps the request pending. It doesn't refuse anything.
plugin_access_dont_allow: Button on a plugin's folder request that refuses it. A refused folder can be asked again via 'Ask again'.
plugin_access_allow_all: Button below several read-only folder requests from one plugin; grants all of them at once.
plugin_access_confirm_title: Title of the console-password dialog that follows pressing 'Allow' on a plugin's folder request.
plugin_access_confirm_body: Body of the 'Allow access?' dialog, above the password field labelled 'Console password'.
plugin_access_ask_again: Button beside a refused folder in a plugin's access list; forgets the refusal so the plugin can request the folder again.
plugin_access_decision_failed: Toast, or error in the password dialog, when allowing, refusing or resetting a plugin's folder access didn't go through.
plugin_access_install_emulator: Title of a plugin's request to install an emulator on this host; the folder path shows below. name: the emulator's name.
plugin_access_install_core: Title of a plugin's request to install RetroArch cores (emulation plug-ins); the folder path shows below. name: core names, comma-separated.
plugin_access_saves: Title of a plugin's request to read and restore the save files of emulators; the folder path shows below.
plugin_access_saves_note: Under 'Read and restore emulator saves', above a folder path; 'this folder' is that path.
plugin_access_install: Button on a request to install an emulator or core; grants the folder and installs.
plugin_access_installing: Label of that install button while the install runs.
plugin_access_not_now: Button on an emulator or core install request that declines it. Pairs with 'Install'.
emulators_title: Card title on the Library page, above the emulators the host can install.
emulators_description: Under 'Emulators' on the Library page. A source is a game source; it can ask for an emulator in its access settings.
emulators_managed: Status line of an emulator the host installed itself; a version may follow after a middle dot.
emulators_not_installed: Status line of an emulator that isn't on the host but can be installed.
emulators_not_offered: Status line of an emulator that isn't on the host and can't be installed from here.
emulators_install: Button and menu item on an emulator row; installs the emulator on the host.
emulators_reinstall: Menu item on an emulator row; installs the emulator Punktfunk manages again.
emulators_remove: Red menu item on an emulator row; uninstalls an emulator Punktfunk installed.
emulators_install_failed: Toast when installing an emulator from the Library page fails.
emulators_remove_failed: Toast when removing an emulator from the Library page fails.
emulators_adopt: Menu item on an emulator row; lets the operator point at a copy they installed themselves. Opens a path field.
emulators_adopt_path: Placeholder and screen-reader label of the field for the file path of the emulator's program.
emulators_adopt_add: Button beside the path field, and the confirm button of the password dialog that follows.
emulators_adopt_failed: Error in the password dialog when adding the operator's own copy fails.
emulators_adopt_confirm_title: Title of the password dialog that opens after 'Add'.
emulators_adopt_confirm_body: Body of that password dialog. The console password is the one used to sign in to this console.
emulators_show_absent: Button under the emulator list that reveals the hidden rows. count: how many emulators are hidden.
emulators_hide_absent: Same button as 'Show {count} not installed' once the list is expanded.
library_source_settings: Menu item or icon button in a source row; opens that source's settings dialog.
library_source_settings_title: Title of a source's settings dialog. source: the source's name.
library_source_settings_save: Button in a source's settings dialog, and the submit button of the console password prompt that can follow.
library_source_settings_saved: Toast after a source's settings are saved.
library_source_settings_failed: Toast when saving a source's settings fails. issue: a short reason, from the host or the plugin.
library_source_settings_unreachable: Error inside a source's settings dialog when its form can't load. issue: a short reason.
library_source_settings_refused: Stands in for the reason after '… —' when a source's settings request is refused with none; no final period by design.
library_source_settings_own_page: Text in a source's settings dialog when it has no form here. source: the source's name.
library_source_settings_open_page: Button under '{source} keeps its settings on its own page.' source: the source's name.
library_stream_title: Card title on a game's Launch tab: the stream settings this host sets for the game, whatever device plays it.
library_stream_hint: Under the 'Stream' card title. Devices keep their own settings for anything left at 'Device decides'.
library_stream_source_title: Heading of the stream settings in a game source's settings dialog. source: the source's name, e.g. Lutris.
library_stream_use: Label of the first stream setting: pick a shared override, Custom values, or none.
library_stream_device: Option in every stream setting: the host sets nothing, each device uses its own setting.
library_stream_same_as_source: Option of 'Use' on a game whose source has stream settings: the game follows the source's. source: the source's name, e.g. Lutris.
library_stream_custom: Option of 'Use': this game has its own values, set in the rows below.
library_stream_new: Last option of 'Use', and a button in the 'Shared overrides' dialog; asks for a name, then creates a reusable set of stream settings.
library_stream_resolution: Stream setting: the picture's height, offered as 4K, 1440p, 1080p, 720p.
library_stream_beyond: Checkbox under 'Resolution': the resolution also goes to devices whose screen is smaller, scaled down there.
library_stream_hz: Option of 'Refresh rate', and part of a game's badge. hz: a whole number, e.g. 60.
library_stream_hdr: Stream setting: HDR on or off for this game.
library_stream_hdr_on: Part of the badge on a game's card when the host turns HDR on for it.
library_stream_hdr_off: Part of the badge on a game's card when the host turns HDR off for it.
library_stream_controller: Stream setting: the controller type the game sees.
library_stream_from: Under a stream setting whose value comes from the game's source, not the game. source: the source's name, e.g. Lutris.
library_stream_edit_shared: Link under 'Use' when a shared override is picked; opens it for editing.
library_stream_failed: Toast when a stream setting change is refused and the host gave no reason of its own.
library_stream_shared: Button on the Library page and title of its dialog: named sets of stream settings that many games can use.
library_stream_shared_empty: Empty line in the 'Shared overrides' dialog.
library_stream_name: Field label in the dialogs that create or rename a shared override.
library_stream_new_title: Title of the dialog that asks for a new shared override's name.
library_stream_rename_title: Title of the dialog that renames a shared override.
library_stream_unused: Beside a shared override no game or source uses.
library_stream_used_games: Beside a shared override: how many games use it. count: a whole number.
library_stream_used_sources: Beside a shared override, after the games count: how many sources use it. count: a whole number.
library_stream_delete_title: Title of the confirm dialog for deleting a shared override. name: its name.
library_stream_delete_body: Body of 'Delete {name}?'. count: how many games use the shared override.
library_stream_delete_sources_body: Body of 'Delete {name}?', after the games sentence. count: how many sources use the shared override.
library_stream_select: Toggle button above the game list: checkboxes appear on the games to change many at once.
library_stream_selected: Bar under the game list while selecting. count: how many games are checked.
library_stream_bulk: Placeholder of the chooser in the selection bar; picking a shared override applies it to every checked game.
library_stream_bulk_failed: Toast when some of the checked games couldn't take the shared override. count: how many.
library_migrate_title: Banner heading on the Sources tab, shown only while a built-in store scanner still runs on an older host.
library_migrate_help: Body of the banner under 'Game sources are moving to plugins'. An add-on is a plugin.
library_migrate_install: Button in that banner, one per store. source: the store's name, such as Steam.
library_source_installing: Toast when a source plugin starts installing. title: the plugin's name.
library_source_install_failed: Toast when installing a source plugin fails and the host gave no reason.
library_provider_filter: Item in a source row's ⋯ menu; shows only that source's games and switches to the Games tab.
library_provider_show_all: Item in the same menu while the games are narrowed to that source; undoes it.
library_provider_purge: Item in a source row's menu, or an icon button named by its tooltip; deletes the entries the source synced. Destructive.
library_provider_purge_confirm: Title of the confirm dialog for removing a source's entries. count: number of entries; provider: the source's name.
library_provider_purge_body: Body of that confirm dialog; says the games stay on the host and only the library list changes.
library_provider_purged: Toast after a source's entries are removed. provider: the source's name.
library_provider_purge_failed: Toast when removing a source's entries fails and the host gave no reason.
library_save: Button on a game's page that saves edits; also saves a plugin tab's settings.
library_create: Button on the new-game page that adds the game; a verb.
library_delete: Button or icon label that deletes a custom game; also the confirm button of 'Delete this custom game?'.
library_entry_tab_information: Tab on a game's page: title, description, developer and similar facts.
library_entry_tab_media: Tab on a game's page: cover art and the brand mark.
library_entry_tab_launch: Tab on a game's page: how the game starts and which process the host watches. A noun, not a button.
library_entry_managed_note: Note under the header of a read-only game on its page. source: the name of the source that owns the entry.
library_entry_missing: Page text when the game no longer exists in the library. The link 'Library' follows.
library_entry_leave_title: Confirm dialog title when leaving a game's page with unsaved edits.
library_entry_leave_body: Body of the dialog 'Leave without saving?'.
library_entry_leave_confirm: Confirm button of 'Leave without saving?'; leaves the page and drops the edits.
library_entry_saved: Toast after a game, or a plugin tab's settings, is saved.
library_entry_unsaved: Label in the bar fixed to the bottom of the screen on phones, beside Save, while a game has unsaved edits.
library_entry_password_first: Replaces 'Unsaved changes' in that bottom bar when saving needs the console password; the field is in the page header.
library_entry_no_details: Information tab of a read-only game when its source sent no description or facts.
library_entry_art_failed: Placeholder in an artwork preview when the image can't be loaded.
library_entry_art_after_save: Placeholder in an artwork preview for a file path typed but not yet saved.
library_entry_art_none: Placeholder in an artwork preview when the slot has no image.
library_media_portrait: Artwork slot on the Media tab: the tall 2:3 cover, the game's tile.
library_media_portrait_help: Hint under the 'Portrait' field. An http(s) URL is a web address; the file can also sit on the host.
library_media_hero: Artwork slot on the Media tab: the wide banner behind the title.
library_media_header: Artwork slot on the Media tab: a landscape capsule image. Not a page header.
library_media_header_help: Hint under the 'Header' field. 460×215 is a size in pixels.
library_media_logo: Artwork slot on the Media tab: the game's logo image.
library_entry_icon: Card title and field label on the Media tab: a small icon for a launcher, picked from a list.
library_entry_icon_help: Hint under 'Brand mark'. A launcher tile without cover art shows this icon.
library_entry_icon_none: Option in the 'Brand mark' list: no icon.
library_entry_launch_title: Row label on a read-only game's Launch tab; the value is 'Steam app …', 'Through its source: …' or 'Command: …'.
library_entry_launch_steam: Value under 'How it launches'. id: the Steam app number.
library_entry_launch_exec: Value under 'How it launches'. name: a launch-template name from the source's plugin, an identifier.
library_entry_launch_command: Value under 'How it launches'. command: the shell command.
library_entry_launch_none: Value under 'How it launches' when the entry has no launch of its own.
library_entry_launch_replaced: Follows the current launch description, such as 'Steam app 12345', on an editable game; the typed 'Launch command' takes over.
library_entry_role_launcher: Value of the 'Role' row on a read-only game: the entry opens a launcher.
library_entry_role_game: Value of the 'Role' row on a read-only game: an ordinary game.
library_entry_role: Row label on a read-only game's Launch tab: whether the entry is a game or a launcher.
library_entry_launches: Plural. First part of the stats line under a game's title, joined with ' · '. count: number of launches.
library_entry_play_time: Part of the stats line under a game's title. time: a formatted duration such as '42 min' or '1 hr 12 min'.
library_entry_last_played: Part of the stats line under a game's title. ago: a relative time already localized, such as 'yesterday' or '3 days ago'.
library_entry_prep_title: Card title on the Launch tab: commands the host runs before launch and undoes after. Shown only when there are any.
library_entry_prep_help: Hint under 'Prep commands'. 'The API' is the host's HTTP API, since the console has no editor for them.
library_entry_plugin_offline: Inside a plugin's tab on a game's page when the plugin can't answer. plugin: its name; issue: a short reason.
library_entry_plugin_open: Button in a plugin's tab; opens the plugin's own page for this game. plugin: its name.
library_entry_plugin_save_failed: Toast when saving a plugin tab's settings fails. plugin: its name; issue: a short reason.
plugin_form_json_hint: Under the title of a plugin's settings dialog or tab when its settings can't be drawn as a form; a JSON text box follows.
plugin_form_path_read: Hint under a folder field in a plugin's settings form. plugin: the plugin's name.
plugin_form_path_write: Hint under a folder field in a plugin's settings form. plugin: the plugin's name.
plugin_form_grant_refused: Error toast or red line after saving plugin settings when the host refused one folder; the other settings did save. path: the folder; issue: why, a sentence from the host.
plugin_form_confirm_title: Title of the console-password dialog when saving plugin settings that hand the plugin new folders.
plugin_form_confirm_body: Body of that dialog, above the password field. plugin: the plugin's name.
library_hide_action: Eye-button tooltip and screen-reader label on a game tile, and a button on its page: keeps the title off client devices.
library_unhide_action: Eye-button tooltip and label on a hidden game, and a button on its page; reverses 'Hide from your devices'.
library_hidden_badge: Badge on a hidden game's tile and page, and tooltip on a dimmed launcher chip. A state.
library_badge_not_installed: Badge on a game tile whose files aren't on the host (when the size is unknown), and the same state in the install panel.
library_install_not_installed_size: Status line in the install panel of a game page. size: download size, such as 26 GB.
library_install_on_host: Status line in the install panel of an installed game. size: space on disk, such as 12.3 GB.
library_install_on_host_plain: Status line in the install panel of an installed game when its size is unknown.
library_install_free: Small line in the install panel. free: free disk space on the host, such as 120 GB.
library_install_free_in: Small line in the install panel. free: free disk space, such as 120 GB; folder: the host path the files go into.
library_install_action: Button on a missing game's page; starts downloading it onto the host.
library_install_pause: Button in the install panel and the Downloads card; pauses a download.
library_install_resume: Button in the install panel and the Downloads card; continues a paused download.
library_install_cancel: Button that stops a download; also the confirm button of 'Cancel this download?'.
library_install_retry: Button that restarts a failed download.
library_install_remove: Button on an installed game's page that uninstalls it from the host; also the confirm button of 'Remove {title}?'.
library_install_progress: Part of a download line, joined with ' · '. done, total: formatted sizes such as 12.3 GB.
library_install_so_far: Part of a download line when the total is unknown. done: a formatted size such as 12.3 GB.
library_install_rate: Part of a download line. rate: a formatted size such as 48 MB; '/s' is per second.
library_install_eta_soon: Last part of a download line: the estimate for a download about to finish.
library_install_eta_min: Last part of a download line. minutes: whole minutes.
library_install_eta_hours: Last part of a download line. hours: whole hours; minutes: remaining whole minutes.
library_install_queued: Status of a queued download in the install panel and Downloads card, and the short text on a tile's badge.
library_install_installing: Status while the host installs a finished download, used when the plugin names no phase.
library_install_paused: Status of a paused download, followed by ' · ' and its progress.
library_install_failed: Status in the install panel after a failed download. error: the reason from the host or plugin, often English.
library_install_failed_plain: Status line in the Downloads card for a failed download with no reason.
library_install_failed_toast: Toast when install, pause, cancel or remove is refused and the host gave no reason.
library_install_cancel_confirm: Title of the confirm dialog for canceling a download.
library_install_cancel_body: Body of 'Cancel this download?'. size: the formatted size downloaded so far, such as 1.2 GB.
library_install_remove_confirm: Title of the confirm dialog for uninstalling a game. title: the game's title.
library_install_remove_body: Body of the uninstall confirm dialog. size: the formatted size freed, such as 12.3 GB. 'Saves' are save games.
library_downloads_title: Heading of the Downloads card above the games; lists every download on the host.
library_downloads_total: Beside the Downloads heading. rate: a formatted size such as 48 MB; '/s' is per second.
library_downloads_done: Status line of a finished download in the Downloads card.
library_downloads_canceled: Status line of a canceled download in the Downloads card.
library_install_filter_label: Screen-reader label of the dropdown above the games that filters by install state.
library_install_filter_all: Option of the install-state filter: no filtering.
library_install_filter_installed: Option of the install-state filter: games whose files are on the host.
library_install_filter_missing: Option of the install-state filter: games not installed. count: how many.
library_delete_confirm: Title of the confirm dialog for deleting a custom game.
settings_title: Heading of the console's own Settings page: language, appearance, network access, navigation, sign-out.
settings_language: Card title on the Settings page, above one button per language (their codes, such as EN, DE).
common_loading: Text under a spinner while a page or card loads; also the spinner's screen-reader label.
common_error: Generic error line in a failed card or dialog when the host gave no reason.
common_confirm: Button that confirms a dialog's action when the dialog has no more specific verb.
common_unauthorized: Error line shown instead of a page's content when the console login has expired; the page then redirects to sign-in.
login_title: Card title of the sign-in page.
login_subtitle: Sentence under the sign-in title, followed directly by the link 'Visit the documentation'.
login_docs_link: Link text after 'Don't know what to do?' on the sign-in page; opens the forgotten-password documentation.
login_password: Label of the password field on the sign-in page.
login_error: Inline error on the sign-in page after a wrong password.
login_throttled: Inline error on the sign-in page after too many attempts. when: a relative time such as 'in 30 seconds' or 'in 5 minutes', from the platform.
login_signing_in: Label of the sign-in button while the request runs.
action_logout: Button in the Account card on the Settings page; ends the console sign-in.
settings_logout_failed: Toast on the Settings page when signing out didn't work; the person stays signed in and can retry.
nav_stats: Tab on the Diagnostics page that shows live performance numbers. Short, sits in a tab bar.
nav_diagnostics: Sidebar and phone-menu entry and page title: health checks, logs, performance, controllers.
nav_troubleshooting: Tab on the Diagnostics page that shows the host's logs and health checks. Short, sits in a tab bar.
troubleshooting_subtitle: Subtitle under the Troubleshooting page heading, above the health checks and the log viewer.
diag_checks_title: Card title on the Troubleshooting page, above the list of host health checks.
diag_rerun: Button in the 'Health checks' card; runs every check again.
diag_rerunning: The 'Re-run checks' button while it runs; disabled.
diag_rerun_failed: Toast and error line in the 'Health checks' card when running the checks fails and the host gave no reason.
diag_loading: Line in the 'Health checks' card while the first results load.
diag_all_ok: Line with a green check in the 'Health checks' card when no check needs attention.
diag_unavailable: Replaces the check list when the host runs an older Punktfunk version that can't report health checks.
diag_show_inapplicable: Toggle under the check list; reveals checks that don't apply to this host, such as Windows-only ones on Linux. count: how many.
diag_hide_inapplicable: The same toggle once the checks that don't apply are shown; hides them again.
diag_impact_label: Small caption in an expanded check, above the sentence about what the problem breaks.
diag_remedy_label: Small caption in an expanded check, above the instructions and command that fix it.
diag_relogin_required: Badge under a check's fix: the fix takes effect only after the computer restarts.
diag_copy: Tooltip and screen-reader label of an icon button that copies a fix command to the clipboard.
diag_copied: Toast after the fix command was copied.
diag_copy_failed: Toast when the browser refused clipboard access for the fix command.
diag_status_ok: Badge on a healthy check row. Short; shown in green.
diag_status_inapplicable: Badge on a check that doesn't apply to this host. Short; shown in gray.
diag_severity_critical: Badge on a check that needs attention and is the most serious level. Short; shown in red.
diag_severity_warning: Badge on a check that needs attention, one step below 'Critical'. Short; shown in amber.
diag_severity_info: Badge on a check problem of the lowest level, a heads-up rather than a fault. Short; shown in amber.
diag_attention_title: Headline of the warning card on the Home page. It lists failing health checks, devices waiting for approval and missing game audio.
diag_attention_link: Link at the bottom of that Home warning card; goes to the Troubleshooting page. An arrow follows.
diag_attention_more: Small text beside 'Troubleshooting' in the Home warning card. count: how many further problems are not listed.
diag_takeover_privilege_title: Health check name, bold in its row. Linux: whether the host may stop the display manager (the login screen service) to take over the screen.
diag_virtual_deck_vhci_title: Health check name, bold in its row. Linux: whether virtual game controllers can attach through the kernel's USB/IP port.
diag_uinput_access_title: Health check name, bold in its row. Linux: whether the host may create virtual input devices, which game controllers depend on.
diag_server_conflict_title: Health check name, bold in its row. Another game-streaming server on this machine would clash with Punktfunk over the same ports.
diag_vdisplay_driver_title: Health check name, bold in its row. Windows: the driver that creates virtual monitors for streams.
diag_pad_audio_title: Health check name, bold in its row. Windows: the audio output that plays a game controller's built-in speaker sound.
diag_pad_driver_title: Health check name, bold in its row. Windows: the driver behind virtual game controllers.
diag_encoder_sharing_title: Health check name, bold in its row. NVIDIA GPUs: whether another app is using the GPU's video encoder at the same time.
diag_niri_virtual_outputs_title: Health check name, bold in its row. Whether niri, a Linux window compositor, can create virtual displays. niri is never translated.
logs_title: Card title of the log viewer on the Troubleshooting page.
logs_sources_label: Caption before the row of toggle chips (Host, Plugins, seats, devices) that choose whose logs are shown.
logs_sources_none: Shown in the log viewer's list area when every source chip is switched off.
logs_devices_empty: Hint under the source chips while no client has uploaded logs. 'Send logs to host' is a menu item in the client apps; keep it identical.
logs_source_host: Toggle chip in the log viewer: the log of the Punktfunk host on this machine.
logs_source_plugins: Toggle chip in the log viewer: output from the plugin runner, the separate service that runs plugins.
logs_source_seat: Toggle chip in the log viewer. name: a profile's display name. A seat is a desktop of its own on this machine for one player.
logs_export_all: Button in the Troubleshooting page heading. Downloads one file with all checks and logs, whatever the viewer is filtered to.
logs_export_all_working: The 'Export all' button while the file is being put together; disabled.
logs_export_all_failed: Toast when the 'Export all' file couldn't be created.
logs_empty_plugins: Empty state when only the Plugins chip is selected; a 'Docs' link follows it.
logs_follow: Log viewer toolbar button that turns on following: the list keeps scrolling to the newest line. Text hides on narrow screens; still the screen-reader label.
logs_pause: The same toolbar button while following; stops the list from scrolling to new lines. Text hides on narrow screens; still the screen-reader label.
logs_clear: Item in the log viewer's overflow menu; empties the log list on screen.
logs_search: Placeholder and screen-reader label of the text filter field above the log list.
logs_level: Screen-reader label of the log level picker. Its options DEBUG, INFO, WARN and ERROR are not translated.
logs_empty: Empty state of the log list when the filters match nothing.
logs_dropped: Status line above the log list: the host's log buffer overwrote older lines before the console fetched them.
logs_download: Item in the log viewer's overflow menu, icon only on some widths; saves the lines now shown as a text file.
logs_stalled: Red banner above the log list when fetching new lines fails while older lines are still shown.
logs_share: Item in the log viewer's overflow menu where the device has a system share sheet; shares the lines now shown.
logs_copy: Item in the log viewer's overflow menu where there is no share sheet; copies the lines now shown to the clipboard.
logs_copied: Toast after the clipboard copy done by 'Copy logs to clipboard' succeeded.
logs_share_failed: Toast when sharing or copying the logs failed.
client_logs_manage: Toggle on the Diagnostics logs page that opens a table of log bundles uploaded by client devices. count: number of bundles.
client_logs_col_received: Column header in the uploaded bundles table; the date and time the bundle arrived.
client_logs_col_device: Column header in the uploaded bundles table; the device that sent the bundle.
client_logs_col_size: Column header in the uploaded bundles table; the bundle's file size. The column is narrow.
client_logs_download: Icon-only button on a bundle row (aria-label and tooltip); saves the bundle file.
client_logs_download_failed: Toast when downloading a log bundle failed.
client_logs_delete: Icon-only button on a bundle row (aria-label and tooltip); also the confirm button of the delete dialog.
client_logs_delete_confirm: Title of the confirm dialog for deleting an uploaded log bundle.
client_logs_delete_body: Body of that dialog; the device can upload its log again.
client_logs_delete_failed: Toast when deleting a log bundle failed.
stats_subtitle: Intro line at the top of the Performance page under Diagnostics. A session's timings are recorded, then shown as charts.
stats_capture_title: Card title on the Performance page, above the Start and Stop buttons. A capture is one recorded session.
stats_capture_desc: Intro in the 'Capture' card. To arm = press 'Start capture'; recording then begins with the next session.
stats_recording: Status badge on the 'Capture' card while a capture runs. A state, not an action.
stats_idle: Status badge on the 'Capture' card while no capture runs. A state, not an action.
stats_start: Button on the 'Capture' card that arms the recorder.
stats_stop: Button on the 'Capture' card that ends the capture and writes the recording. '&' is part of the label.
stats_elapsed: Label above a time such as 2:35 on the 'Capture' card: how long the capture has run.
stats_samples: Label above a number on the 'Capture' card: samples recorded so far. A sample summarises one or two seconds of stream.
stats_kind: Label above a value on the 'Capture' card: which streaming path is recorded. Values: 'Native', 'GameStream', 'Browser'.
stats_kind_native: Value of 'Path', also a badge in the recordings table: Punktfunk's own protocol and clients.
stats_kind_gamestream: Value of 'Path', also a badge in the recordings table: the GameStream-compatible path. Product name, keep.
stats_kind_web: Value of 'Path', also a badge in the recordings table: a session from the browser client.
stats_live_title: Card title of the live charts, shown only while a capture runs.
stats_live_window: Footnote under the live charts once the capture outgrows the plotted window. count: number of newest samples plotted.
stats_live_waiting: Empty state in the 'Live' card right after 'Start capture', until the first samples arrive.
stats_latency_title: Chart title, in the live card and in a recording's detail: time each frame spends in each pipeline stage.
stats_latency_axis: Unit on the latency chart's vertical axis, written after a number: milliseconds.
