stats_latency_desc: Description under 'Latency by stage'. 'The host's whole share' is the time from screen capture to the last packet sent.
stats_throughput_title: Chart title: frame rate and data rate over time, against the stream's targets.
stats_health_title: Chart title: counts of lost and recovered frames and packets over time.
stats_fps_new: Legend entry on the throughput chart: frames per second that carried new picture content.
stats_fps_repeat: Legend entry on the throughput chart: frames per second that repeated the last picture because the screen did not change.
stats_mbps: Legend entry on the throughput chart: measured data rate in megabits per second. The unit is part of the label.
stats_bitrate_target: Legend entry on the throughput chart: the data rate the encoder aims for, in megabits per second.
stats_p99: Toggle button above the latency chart: plot the 99th percentile, the slow frames. Pairs with 'p50'; keep it short.
stats_p50: Toggle button above the latency chart: plot the median, the 50th percentile. Pairs with 'p99'; keep it short.
stats_frames_dropped: Legend entry on the 'Health' chart: frames the host dropped in the sample window.
stats_packets_dropped: Legend entry on the 'Health' chart: network packets lost on the way, counted by the client.
stats_send_dropped: Legend entry on the 'Health' chart: packets the host could not send because its send buffer was full.
stats_fec_recovered: Legend entry on the 'Health' chart: lost packets the client rebuilt with forward error correction (FEC).
stats_recordings_title: Card title of the table of saved captures on the Performance page.
stats_recordings_empty: Empty state of the recordings table. 'Start capture' is the button on the card above.
stats_col_time: Table column header: when the recording started, a date and time.
stats_col_kind: Table column header: the streaming path. Values: 'Native', 'GameStream', 'Browser'.
stats_col_resolution: Table column header: picture size and frame rate, such as 2560×1440@60.
stats_col_codec: Table column header: the video codec, such as HEVC or AV1.
stats_col_duration: Narrow, right-aligned table column header: the recording's length, such as 1:30.
stats_col_samples: Narrow, right-aligned table column header: how many samples the recording holds.
stats_view: Icon button on a recording row (tooltip and screen-reader name): shows that recording's charts below the table.
stats_download: Icon-only menu item on a recording row: saves the recording to the computer as a JSON file.
stats_delete: Icon-only menu item on a recording row, and the confirm button of 'Delete this recording?'.
stats_delete_confirm: Title of the confirm dialog before deleting a saved recording.
stats_delete_body: Body of the confirm dialog 'Delete this recording?'.
stats_detail_title: Card title above the charts of the recording picked in the table. The mode and encoder follow it.
stats_close: Screen-reader label of the icon-only X button that closes the recording detail card.
stats_no_samples: Empty state in the recording detail card when the saved recording holds no data.
stats_frame_budget: Label on the dashed line of the latency chart: how long one frame lasts at the stream's rate. ms: milliseconds, such as 8.3.
stats_fps_budget: Label on the dashed line of the throughput chart: the stream's frame rate. fps: frames per second, such as 60.
stats_host_total: Legend entry on the latency chart for the line showing the host's whole time per frame, from capture to sent.
stats_rtt_title: Chart title and its one series name: round-trip time of the network link between host and client.
stats_send_title: Chart title: time spent preparing each frame for sending, split into error correction, encryption and socket.
stats_send_fec: Legend entry on 'Sealing per frame': time to compute the error-correction data (FEC) added to a frame.
stats_send_seal: Legend entry on 'Sealing per frame': time to encrypt a frame's packets.
stats_send_sock: Legend entry on 'Sealing per frame': time to hand the packets to the network socket.
stats_truncated_note: Note at the top of a recording's charts when the capture hit its size limit and stopped storing samples.
stats_health_none: Shown in place of the 'Health' chart when the recorded path counts no losses.
stats_col_encoder: Table column header: the video encoder backend used, such as nvenc or vaapi. Hidden on narrow screens.
stats_stage_queue: Pipeline stage in the latency chart's legend: time a frame waits in a queue before processing.
stats_stage_capture: Pipeline stage in the latency chart's legend: grabbing the screen image.
stats_stage_submit: Pipeline stage in the latency chart's legend: handing the frame to the video encoder.
stats_stage_encode: Pipeline stage in the latency chart's legend: compressing the frame into video.
stats_stage_driver: Pipeline stage in the latency chart's legend: the virtual display driver's capture and encode time, as one block.
stats_stage_packetize: Pipeline stage in the latency chart's legend: cutting the encoded frame into network packets.
stats_stage_copy: Pipeline stage in the latency chart's legend: copying the encoded frame into the send buffer.
stats_stage_send: Pipeline stage in the latency chart's legend: putting the packets on the network.
stats_stage_send_spread: Pipeline stage in the latency chart's legend: the time over which one frame's packets are paced out.
stats_stage_pool: Pipeline stage in the latency chart's legend: time a frame waits for a free buffer in the driver's pool.
stats_stage_ipc: Pipeline stage in the latency chart's legend: passing the encoded frame from the driver to the host process.
store_title: Title of the Plugins page, where plugins are browsed, installed and removed.
store_subtitle: Line under the Plugins page title. Catalogs are the plugin lists managed on the Sources tab.
store_tab_browse: Tab on the Plugins page that lists plugins from the catalogs, ready to install.
store_tab_installed: Tab on the Plugins page that lists plugins installed on this host. A count badge may follow it.
store_tab_sources: Tab on the Plugins page that lists the plugin catalogs and lets the operator add one.
store_tier_verified: Badge on a plugin from the built-in unom catalog, which unom reviewed. Also the screen-reader label of a check icon.
store_tier_external: Badge on a plugin from a catalog the operator added. unom didn't review it.
store_tier_unverified: Badge, in a warning color, on a plugin installed from a raw package name with no catalog.
store_tier_cli: Badge on a plugin installed from the command line, so the host doesn't know where it came from.
store_tier_cli_hint: Tooltip of the 'Installed via CLI' badge.
store_from_source: Small label directly before a catalog's name, as in 'from <name>'; the name is a separate element after it.
store_search_placeholder: Placeholder and screen-reader label of the search field on the Browse tab.
store_filter_all: Filter button on the Browse tab that shows plugins from every catalog; one button per catalog name sits beside it.
store_category_all: Filter button on the Browse tab that shows every plugin group; group buttons such as 'Game sources' sit beside it.
store_category_tools: Group heading and filter button on the Browse tab for utility plugins that aren't game or art sources.
store_category_other: Group heading and filter button on the Browse tab for plugins that fit no other group.
store_all_sources_failed: Empty state on the Browse tab when no catalog could be loaded. sources: catalog names, comma-separated.
store_empty: Empty state on the Browse tab when the catalogs list no plugins.
store_no_match: Empty state on the Browse tab when the search and filters match no plugin.
store_by_author: Small line under a plugin's name on its Browse card, followed by ' · v1.2.0'. author: the author's name.
store_homepage: Link on a Browse card to the plugin's website.
store_install: Button on a Browse card that starts installing the plugin after a confirm dialog.
store_installed_label: State text with a check icon that replaces the Install button on a Browse card when the plugin is already installed.
store_update_to: Button on a Browse card or Installed row that installs a newer version. version: the new version number, such as 1.4.0.
store_incompatible: Amber warning on a Browse card when this host can't run the plugin and no more specific reason is given.
store_blocked: Red notice on a plugin card or installed row: the host blocks this plugin. reason: a sentence from the host, often English.
store_spec_open: Quiet link at the bottom of the Browse tab; opens a dialog to install a package by its registry name, outside any catalog.
store_runner_title: Title of the card on the Installed tab for the plugin runner, the background service all plugins run inside.
store_runner_help: Text in the Plugin runner card when the service is installed.
store_runner_not_installed: Text in the Plugin runner card when the service is missing from this host; replaces the help text.
store_runner_banner: Amber banner on the Browse tab when the plugin runner is switched off; 'Enable runner' sits beside it. The host's own sentence can replace it.
store_runner_enable: Button in the runner banner and card that starts the plugin runner and keeps it on.
store_runner_disable: Button in the Plugin runner card that stops the service, and so every plugin, without uninstalling any.
store_runner_state_running: Badge in the Plugin runner card: the service is up.
store_runner_state_stopped: Badge in the Plugin runner card: the service is switched on but isn't up right now.
store_runner_state_disabled: Badge in the Plugin runner card: the operator switched the service off.
store_runner_state_missing: Badge in the Plugin runner card: the service isn't installed on this host.
store_runner_unit: Label of a label/value pair in the runner card; the value is the service's system name, such as punktfunk-scripting.
store_runner_principal: Label of a label/value pair in the runner card; the value is the OS account the service runs under.
store_runner_failed: Error toast when switching the plugin runner on or off didn't work.
store_installed_title: Title of the card on the Installed tab that lists the installed plugins.
store_installed_empty: Empty state in the Installed card.
store_running: State in an installed plugin's row: its process is up. ' · ' and the version follow.
store_stopped: State in an installed plugin's row: its process isn't up. ' · ' and the version follow.
store_version_unknown: Replaces the version number in an installed plugin's row when none is known; follows ' · ' after the running state.
store_uninstall: Row action (trash icon, shown as tooltip and screen-reader label) and confirm button that removes a plugin from the host.
store_uninstall_confirm: Title of the confirm dialog for removing a plugin. title: the plugin's name.
store_uninstall_failed: Error toast when the host didn't accept the request to remove a plugin.
store_update_no_entry: Error toast after pressing Update on an installed plugin whose catalog entry can't be found. A refresh re-reads the catalogs.
store_update_all_count: Button above the Installed list that updates every plugin with a newer catalog version. count: number of plugins to update.
store_updates_pending: Screen-reader-only text beside the number badge on the 'Installed' tab. count: number of plugins with an update.
store_update_all_title: Title of the confirm dialog opened by 'Update all'; a list of old and new versions follows.
store_update_all_body: Body of that dialog. 'Plugin runner' is the service shown on the Installed tab.
store_update_all_external_note: Amber warning in that dialog when some updates come from catalogs the operator added. sources: catalog names, comma-separated.
store_update_all_confirm: Confirm button of the 'Update these plugins?' dialog.
store_update_all_external_confirm: Confirm button of that dialog instead of 'Update all' when the amber warning shows; 'anyway' acknowledges it.
store_update_all_skipped: Small note in that dialog about plugins that won't be updated. names: plugin names, comma-separated.
store_update_all_step: Progress line on the install card while Update all runs, such as 'Update 2 of 5'. index: current number; total: how many.
store_update_all_running: Title of the progress card in the gap between two updates of an Update all run; 'Update {index} of {total}' sits under it.
store_update_all_finished: Success toast when an Update all run ends. count: number of plugins updated.
store_update_all_stopped: Error toast when an Update all run stops at the first failure. done: plugins updated; left: plugins not updated, including the failed one.
store_sources_title: Title of the card on the Sources tab that lists the plugin catalogs.
store_sources_help: Text in the Sources card. unom is the publisher of Punktfunk and of the built-in catalog.
store_refresh_all: Button in the Sources card that re-fetches every catalog.
store_refresh_failed: Error toast when re-fetching the catalogs didn't work.
store_source_builtin: Badge with a lock icon on the built-in catalog in the Sources list.
store_source_signed: Badge on a catalog whose index the host checks against a public key.
store_source_unsigned: Badge, in a warning color, on a catalog added without a public key, so its index can't be checked for tampering.
store_source_stale: Badge, in a warning color, on a catalog whose last fetch failed, so the host shows the last good copy.
store_source_entries: Count in a catalog's row on the Sources tab, before ' · last fetched …'. count: number of plugins it lists.
store_source_fetched: After the plugin count in a catalog's row. when: a formatted date and time, or the word 'never'.
store_source_never: Fills 'last fetched {when}' for a catalog that has never been fetched, so it reads mid-sentence.
store_source_remove: Trash button (screen-reader label) on an added catalog's row, and the confirm button of its remove dialog.
store_source_remove_confirm: Title of the confirm dialog for removing a catalog. name: the catalog's name, chosen by the operator.
store_source_remove_failed: Error toast when removing a catalog didn't work.
store_source_builtin_locked: Error toast when the host refuses to remove the built-in catalog.
store_add_source_title: Title of the card on the Sources tab with the form to add a catalog.
store_field_source_name: Label of the field for the name the operator gives a new catalog.
store_field_source_url: Label of the field for the web address of a catalog's index file.
store_field_source_key: Label of an optional field for the catalog's public signing key.
store_field_source_key_help: Hint under the public key field. 'ed25519:…' is the literal key prefix; keep it as is.
store_add_source: Submit button of the add-catalog form; a trust dialog opens next.
store_add_source_failed: Error line in the 'Trust this source?' dialog when the host rejects the new catalog.
store_source_trust_title: Title of the dialog, with a warning icon, that asks the operator to trust a newly added catalog.
store_source_trust_body: Body of that dialog, above the catalog's address. name: the catalog's name.
store_source_trust_unsigned: Amber warning in that dialog when no public key was entered.
store_source_trust_confirm: Submit button of the trust dialog, pressed after typing the console password; a deliberate acknowledgement.
store_install_title: Title of the confirm dialog for installing a plugin from the built-in catalog. title: the plugin's name.
store_install_verified_body: Body of that dialog. version: the version number, such as 1.2.0.
store_install_confirm: Confirm button of the install dialog for a plugin from the built-in catalog.
store_install_external_title: Title of the confirm dialog for installing a plugin from a catalog the operator added. title: the plugin's name.
store_install_external_body: Body of that dialog. version: such as 1.2.0; source: the name of the added catalog.
store_install_external_note: Amber warning in the 'Install {title} from an external source?' dialog.
store_install_external_confirm: Confirm button of that dialog; 'anyway' acknowledges the amber warning.
store_install_failed: Error toast when the host didn't start an install or update.
store_busy: Error toast, in place of an install or removal error, when the host is already running another plugin job.
store_spec_title: Title of the dialog, with a red warning icon, for installing a plugin from a raw package spec (a registry package name and version).
store_spec_lead: Body of that dialog: a warning that nobody reviewed the code. 'Plugin runner' is the service shown on the Installed tab.
store_spec_permanent: Red notice in the package-spec dialog. 'Unverified' is the text of the trust badge of this kind of install.
store_spec_field: Label of the field where the package spec is typed.
store_spec_field_help: Hint under the package spec field. The example is a literal package name; keep it as is.
store_spec_confirm_field: Label of a second field in the package-spec dialog; typing the spec again is a safeguard against a slip.
store_spec_checkbox: Checkbox label in the package-spec dialog that must be ticked to proceed. Operator privileges: the access the plugin runner has on this host.
store_spec_confirm: Red submit button of the package-spec dialog; installs the plugin as 'Unverified'.
store_spec_password: Label of every console-password field (package spec, adding a catalog, allowing folders, pairing). The console password is the one used to sign in to this web console.
store_spec_password_help: Hint under the password field in the package-spec dialog.
store_job_install: Title of the progress card while a plugin installs or updates. target: the plugin or package name.
store_job_uninstall: Title of the progress card while a plugin is removed. target: the plugin or package name.
store_job_done_install: Status line on the progress card after a successful install or update.
store_job_done_uninstall: Status line on the progress card after a successful removal.
store_job_failed: Status line on the progress card after a failed install or removal; the host's error text follows in a red box.
store_job_restarting: Note on the progress card after a successful job. 'Plugin runner' is the background service; the sidebar lists plugins that have a page.
store_job_lost: Title of a card when the console can no longer get the status of an install or removal job.
store_job_lost_hint: Under 'Lost track of this job'. 'Installed' is the Installed tab.
store_job_log: Collapsible heading on the progress card that reveals the job's log, which is command output.
store_job_dismiss: Close (X) button on a finished job's card or a lost-job card. Screen-reader label only.
store_phase_queued: Status line on the progress card: the job waits to start.
store_phase_verifying: Status line on the progress card: the package is being checked before it's installed.
store_phase_installing: Status line on the progress card: the package is being installed.
store_phase_removing: Status line on the progress card: the package is being removed.
store_phase_checking: Status line on the progress card: the host checks the finished install.
store_phase_rolling_back: Status line on the progress card: the install failed and the earlier state is being restored.
store_phase_recording: Status line on the progress card: the host saves where the package came from (its provenance).
store_phase_restarting: Status line on the progress card: the plugin runner service is being restarted so the plugin starts.
store_job_walk: Line under the progress card's status while the host sets folder access, which takes minutes on a large Windows folder. path: the folder; seconds: whole seconds so far.
store_phase_done: Status line on the progress card for the last step, shown briefly before the job's final state.
games_state_launching: Badge on a game row on Home: the host is starting the game.
games_state_running: Badge on a game row on Home: the game is up and running.
games_state_exited: Badge on a game row on Home: the game has quit.
games_state_grace: Red badge on a game row on Home: the client left, and the host holds the game open for a countdown in case it returns.
games_state_untracked: Badge on a game row on Home: the host can't tell when this game ends, so the session doesn't follow it.
games_state_detached: Badge on a game row on Home: the game still runs but no client is streaming it.
games_detached_note: Detail line on a game row on Home, under the badge 'Nobody streaming'.
games_untracked_note: Detail line on a game row on Home, under the badge 'Not tracked'.
games_closing_in: Detail line on a game row on Home, under the badge 'Waiting for client'. time: a countdown such as 1:23.
games_end_all_waiting_confirm: Body of the confirm dialog titled 'End all {count} games nobody is streaming?'. count: number of such games.
games_end_all_waiting_title: Title of a confirm dialog on Home before ending several games at once. count: number of games nobody is streaming.
action_stop_session_all_confirm: Body of the 'Stop every live session?' dialog on the Home page. count: number of live sessions, at least 2.
action_stop_session_all_title: Title of the confirm dialog on the Home page when Stop would end every session on the host.
action_stop_session_all: Red confirm button of 'Stop every live session?'.
games_end_now: Button on a game row on Home and confirm button of its dialog; closes the game on the host at once.
session_game_on_exit: Row label in Host settings, Session category. A segmented choice for what the streaming session does when its launched game quits.
session_game_on_exit_help: Hint under the 'When the game exits' row. The library is the game list inside the client app.
session_game_on_exit_end: Option of 'When the game exits': the streaming session stops. Short, in a segmented control.
session_game_on_exit_keep: Option of 'When the game exits': the session stays up after the game quits. Short, in a segmented control.
session_game_end_game: Row label in Host settings, Session category. A segmented choice for what happens to a game the host launched once its session ends.
session_game_end_game_help: Hint under the 'When the session ends' row. 'Never one you started yourself' means a game started by hand on the machine.
session_game_end_keep: Option of 'When the session ends': the game keeps running. Short, in a segmented control.
session_game_end_on_quit: Option of 'When the session ends': close the game only when the player stops the session on purpose, not when the connection drops.
session_game_end_always: Option of 'When the session ends': close the game on any end. After a dropped connection it waits for the 'Reconnect window' first.
session_game_always_warning: Warning under the 'When the session ends' row, shown only while 'Always close it' is selected.
session_game_new_launch: Row label in Host settings, Session category. What happens to the game still running when the same device starts a different one.
session_game_new_launch_help: Hint under the 'When you launch another game' row.
session_game_new_launch_keep: Option of 'When you launch another game': the earlier game keeps running. Short, in a segmented control.
session_game_new_launch_end: Option of 'When you launch another game': the earlier game is closed before the new one starts. Short, in a segmented control.
session_game_new_launch_scope: Note under the 'When you launch another game' row, shown only while 'Close it first' is selected.
session_game_grace: Label and screen-reader label of a number field in seconds, shown only with 'Always close it'. Time a dropped client has to come back.
session_game_saved: Toast after any change in the Session game rows is saved.
session_game_nested_note: Note under 'When the session ends'. 'Keep alive' is a display setting: how long a virtual display outlives a disconnect. gamescope is never translated.
display_monitor_env_locked: Amber notice at the top of 'Screens'. PUNKTFUNK_CAPTURE_MONITOR is an environment variable name; keep it as is.
display_monitor_primary: Small badge on a monitor row in 'Screens', and screen-reader label of a star on the map: the main monitor.
display_monitor_disabled: Small badge on a monitor row in 'Screens': the monitor is switched off. Keep it very short.
display_monitor_missing: Red badge on the row of a monitor chosen for streaming that is no longer connected to the host.
display_monitor_missing_hint: Detail line under the name of a missing monitor in 'Screens'. 'No client' means any device trying to connect.
display_monitor_missing_warning: Red warning at the top of 'Screens'. 'The virtual screen' is the button 'Give each device its own screen'.
update_title: Card title on the Host page for updating the host software.
update_available_badge: Badge in the Updates card header, and the status line in the Host page strip, when a newer version exists.
update_current: Row label in the Updates card; the value is the host's installed version number with badges.
update_install_kind: Tooltip of a badge that shows how the host was installed, such as apt or windows-installer.
update_latest: Row label in the Updates card; the value is the newest published version number.
update_notes: Link beside the latest version number; opens its release notes in a new tab.
update_up_to_date: Line in the Updates card when the host runs the newest version.
update_how: Lead-in ending with a colon, above a shell command the admin copies and runs on the host.
update_check_now: Button in the Updates card; asks the update feed whether a newer version exists.
update_checking: The 'Check now' button while it runs; also the Host page strip's 'Check for update' button while it runs.
update_last_checked: Label before a date and time, as in 'Last checked 7 Nov 2026, 14:03:05'; the date follows after a space.
update_never_checked: Value of the 'Latest release' row when no update check has finished yet.
update_none_published: Value of the 'Latest release' row when the update channel has no release yet.
update_not_published: Paragraph in the Updates card. channel: the update channel's name as in its badge, such as stable or canary.
update_stale: Amber warning in the Updates card. git.unom.io is the project's server address and stays as is.
update_disabled: Shown in place of the 'Check now' button. PUNKTFUNK_UPDATE_CHECK=0 is a setting and stays as is.
update_error: Toast when an update check fails, and the start of a red line in the Updates card; ' — ' and the host's reason follow there.
update_copy: Button beside a shell command; copies the command to the clipboard.
update_copied: The 'Copy' button for two seconds after the command was copied.
update_apply_ready: Line in the Updates card when the console can install the update itself. version: the new version number, such as 0.47.0.
update_apply_button: Button in the Updates card that starts the update; also the confirm button in its password dialog. Short.
update_apply_confirm_title: Title of the password dialog opened by 'Update now'. version: the new version number, such as 0.47.0.
update_apply_confirm_body: Body of the password dialog opened by 'Update now'. The console password is the one used to sign in to this web console.
update_apply_force_warning: Replaces the dialog body when a stream is live. 'This page' is the web console, which may itself be viewed through the stream.
update_apply_force_button: Red confirm button of that dialog, replacing 'Update now' while a stream is live.
update_apply_wrong_password: Error under the password field of the update dialog.
update_apply_throttled: Error under the password field of a dialog, and toast after 'Check now' when the host limits repeat requests.
update_apply_working: Label of the dialog's confirm button while the update request is sent.
update_apply_give_up: Button in the amber timeout warning; stops waiting for the host to come back.
update_apply_timeout: Amber warning in the progress panel. The log path at the end is a file pattern and stays as is.
update_applying_title: Heading of the update progress panel. version: the version being installed.
update_stage_downloading: Progress line while downloading. pct: whole number from 0 to 100; the percent sign follows it.
update_stage_downloading_indeterminate: Progress line while downloading when the total size is unknown, so there is no percentage.
update_stage_verifying: Progress line: the downloaded installer is checked for integrity before it runs.
update_stage_applying: Progress line: the downloaded installer takes over and replaces the host's files.
update_stage_restarting: Progress line: the host program restarts itself after the update.
update_stage_reconnecting: Progress line while the console can't reach the host, as expected during a restart.
update_result_ok: Success line in the Updates card after an update. from, to: version numbers; the arrow is part of the text.
update_result_staged: Success line on hosts that finish installing at the next reboot. to: the new version number.
update_result_noop: Line after an update that changed nothing because the host's package repository had no newer version yet.
update_result_noop_source: Line after an update on a host built from source (Steam Deck) that changed nothing.
update_opt_in: Lead-in ending with a colon, above a shell command that enables one-click updates from the console.
update_result_failed: Red heading in the Updates card. to: target version number; stage: the step that failed, in English as the host names it, or ? if unknown.
update_result_log: Label before the file path of the installer log; the path follows after a space.
library_field_role: Checkbox label on the Launch tab. A launcher is an entry that opens a store app, not a game.
library_field_role_help: Hint under 'This entry opens a launcher'. The Launchers row sits above the games.
library_field_audio: Group title and screen-reader label of the dropdown on the Launch tab, choosing which clients hear the game.
library_field_audio_help: Hint under that dropdown. 'Session card' is where a running stream is shown and muted.
library_audio_all: Option of 'Who hears this title': every client on the shared display.
library_audio_owner: Option of 'Who hears this title': only the client that owns the shared display.
library_audio_joined: Option of 'Who hears this title': only clients that joined another's display.
library_audio_launcher: Option of 'Who hears this title': only the client whose session started the game.
docs_link: Link text at the end of a hint; opens the documentation site in a new tab. An arrow icon follows.
store_all_platforms: Checkbox on the Browse tab that also lists plugins this host's operating system can't run; shown only when some are hidden.
nav_home_hint: Second line under 'Home' in the phone's More menu; says what the page is for. One line, may be cut off.
nav_diagnostics_hint: Second line under 'Diagnostics' in the phone's More menu; says what the page holds. One line, may be cut off.
nav_devices_hint: Second line under 'Devices' in the phone's More menu; says what the page is for. One line, may be cut off.
nav_displays_hint: Second line under 'Displays' in the phone's More menu; says what the page controls. One line, may be cut off.
nav_library_hint: Second line under 'Library' in the phone's More menu; says what the page holds. One line, may be cut off.
nav_host_hint: Second line under 'Host' in the phone's More menu; lists what the page holds. One line, may be cut off.
nav_automation_hint: Second line under 'Automation' in the phone's More menu; says what the page is for. One line, may be cut off.
nav_plugins_hint: Second line under 'Plugins' in the phone's More menu; says what the page is for. One line, may be cut off.
nav_settings_hint: Second line under 'Settings' in the phone's More menu; lists what the page holds. One line, may be cut off.
nav_group_manage: Group heading above the secondary pages (Diagnostics, Automation, Plugins, Settings) in the sidebar and phone menu.
nav_group_pinned: Group heading above the plugin pages the operator pinned, in the sidebar and phone menu.
nav_pin: Button on a plugin's page that adds the plugin to the sidebar; also its tooltip and screen-reader label. Small screens show it as an icon.
nav_unpin: Button on a plugin's page that removes the plugin from the sidebar; also its tooltip and screen-reader label.
settings_navigation: Card title on the Settings page, above checkboxes that pin plugin pages to the sidebar.
settings_navigation_help: Under 'Navigation'. A plugin is an add-on that brings its own page; pinned means listed in the left sidebar.
plugin_installed_toast: Success toast when a plugin with its own page first appears on the host. name: the plugin's title. 'Plugins' is the sidebar entry; 'pin' is 'Pin to sidebar'.
settings_reach_title: Card title on the Settings page, shown only when other devices on the network can open this web console.
settings_reach_lan: Body of the 'Network access' card, a warning. url: this page's address, such as http://192.168.1.20:3000.
settings_reach_change: Under the 'Network access' warning. Keep PUNKTFUNK_UI_BIND=127.0.0.1 and host.env exactly as written.
settings_account: Card title on the Settings page, above the sign-out button.
display_says_mirror: Summary sentence when one real monitor is streamed to every device. connector: the monitor's system name, such as DP-1.
display_says_mirror_device: Same sentence for one device, in its display sheet. name: the device's name; connector: the monitor's system name, such as DP-1.
display_says_each_extend: First sentence of the Displays page summary and of preset captions: the device gets an extra screen beside the host's real monitors.
display_says_each_primary: First sentence of the Displays page summary and of preset captions: the device's screen becomes the desktop's main screen.
display_says_each_exclusive: First sentence of the Displays page summary and of preset captions: the device's screen is the only one and the host's monitors switch off.
display_says_each_auto: First sentence of the Displays page summary and of preset captions: the host picks the layout itself.
display_says_device_extend: Same sentence in one device's display sheet: the device gets an extra screen beside the host's real monitors. name: the device's name.
display_says_device_primary: Same sentence in one device's display sheet: the device's screen becomes the desktop's main screen. name: the device's name.
display_says_device_exclusive: Same sentence in one device's display sheet: the device's screen is the only one and the host's monitors switch off. name: the device's name.
display_says_device_auto: Same sentence in one device's display sheet: the host picks the layout itself. name: the device's name.
display_says_on_disconnect_remove: Second sentence of the Displays summary: the device's screen is deleted when it disconnects.
display_says_on_disconnect_keep: Second sentence of the Displays summary: the device's screen stays a while. seconds: a whole number.
display_says_on_disconnect_forever: Second sentence of the Displays summary: the screen stays until 'Release' is pressed.
display_says_second_separate: Sentence in the policy summary: what happens when another device connects while one is already streaming.
display_says_second_steal: Sentence in the policy summary: the second device replaces the first one's session.
display_says_second_join: Sentence in the policy summary: the second device watches the same screen as the first.
display_says_second_reject: Sentence in the policy summary: the second device is refused because the host is in use.
display_says_game_dedicated: Sentence added to the policy summary when 'Dedicated' game sessions are chosen.
display_says_next_connect: Sentence added to the policy summary while a session streams: a change takes effect only for the next connection.
display_map_label: Screen-reader label of the desktop map on the Displays page, a picture of monitors and device screens drawn to scale.
display_map_unnamed: Name shown for a device screen whose device has no known name, on the map and in 'Screens'.
display_map_streamed: Button label on a monitor row in 'Screens' once that monitor is the streamed one; also a map icon's screen-reader label. Contrast 'Stream this monitor'.
display_map_empty: Empty state on the Displays page, in the map card and in 'Screens', when there are no monitors or device screens.
display_release: Button on the row of a kept device screen in 'Screens'. Removes the screen kept after its device left.
display_state_streaming: State word on a device's screen, on the map and in 'Screens': a session is using it now.
display_state_kept: State word on a device's screen: the device has disconnected and the screen stays for now.
display_state_kept_until: State word on a device's screen: kept with no timer, until the user releases it.
display_customise: Last preset card on the Displays page, and the title of the dialog it opens with one question per setting.
display_customise_desc: Line under 'Customise' on its preset card.
display_q_keep: Question label in Customise and in a device's sheet: what happens to a device's screen after it disconnects.
display_q_keep_off: Option under 'After a device disconnects'. Also names this choice in a device's one-line summary.
display_q_keep_for: Option under 'After a device disconnects'. A number field and 'seconds' follow it, so it reads 'Keep for [10] seconds'.
display_q_keep_forever: Option under 'After a device disconnects': the screen stays until 'Release' is pressed.
display_q_monitors: Question label in Customise and in a device's sheet: what the host's real monitors do while a device streams.
display_q_monitors_extend: Option under 'Your monitors while streaming': they stay on, the device's screen is added. Also a per-monitor choice in 'Screens'.
display_q_monitors_primary: Option under 'Your monitors while streaming': they stay on, and the device's screen becomes the main screen.
display_q_monitors_exclusive: Option under 'Your monitors while streaming': they switch off. Also a per-monitor choice in 'Screens'.
display_q_monitors_auto: Option under 'Your monitors while streaming': the host picks what suits this machine.
display_q_second: Question label in Customise and in a device's sheet: what happens when another device connects while one is streaming.
display_q_second_separate: Option under 'A second device connects': each device has its own virtual screen.
display_q_second_steal: Option under 'A second device connects': the new device ends the current device's session.
display_q_second_join: Option under 'A second device connects': both devices see the same screen.
display_q_second_reject: Option under 'A second device connects': the new device is refused because the host is busy.
display_q_remember: Question label in Customise and in a device's sheet: whether the desktop keeps display settings, such as scaling, per device.
display_q_remember_shared: Option under 'Remember display settings': one set of settings for all devices.
display_q_remember_client: Option under 'Remember display settings': a separate set for each device.
display_q_remember_mode: Option under 'Remember display settings': a separate set for each device at each resolution.
display_q_remember_help: Hint under 'Remember display settings'. The desktop is the host's own desktop environment.
display_q_max: Label of a number field (1 to 16) under 'Advanced', also its screen-reader label: how many device screens can exist at once.
display_screens: Card title on the Displays page: the list of the host's monitors and the screens streamed to devices.
display_turns_off: Plain text on a monitor row in 'Screens': this monitor switches off while a device streams.
display_when_connects: Card title on the Displays page above the policy summary and the preset cards.
display_next_device: Label inside the dashed placeholder box on the map: where the next device's screen would appear. Not a real device.
display_arrange_auto: Button under 'Advanced', shown only after the user dragged screens on the map. Returns to automatic placement.
display_other_desktops: Card title on the Displays page listing the desktops of other profiles with a seat of their own.
display_desktop_of: Row title in 'Other desktops'. name: a profile's display name.
display_seats_contract: Hint under 'Other desktops'. owner: the owner profile's name, or 'This host' if none.
display_advanced: Heading of the collapsed section at the bottom of the Displays page. Click to open.
display_arranged_by_you: Sentence appended to the policy summary, and label of a field under 'Advanced', when screens were placed by hand on the map.
display_arrange_hint: Hint under the desktop map when two or more device screens exist.
display_stream_this: Button on a monitor row in 'Screens'. Streams this real monitor to every device instead of a virtual screen.
display_stream_virtual: Button on the row of a missing monitor in 'Screens'. Stops streaming it; each device gets its own virtual screen again.
display_stream_this_hint: Hint at the top of 'Screens'. The button is 'Stream this monitor'; 'press again' toggles it off.
display_state_kept_for: Chip on a kept device screen, and entry in a device's one-line summary. seconds: whole seconds left, or the keep time set.
display_save: Button on the Automation page's unsaved-changes bar, and the submit button of its password dialog. Saves the hook list.
display_revert: Button on the Automation page's unsaved-changes bar. Throws away edits to the hook list.
display_follows_host: Summary in the Display column of a paired device's row when it has no settings of its own.
display_follow_host: First option under each question in a device's display sheet. May be followed by ' · ' and the host's current answer.
display_follow_host_all: Ghost button at the bottom of a device's display sheet. Clears all of that device's own settings.
display_device_settings: Opens a device's display sheet. Button in a device's Display column, and screen-reader label of the gear icon on its screen.
display_mirrors: Part of a device's one-line display summary (parts joined by ' · '). connector: the monitor's system name, such as DP-1.
settings_appearance: Card title on the Settings page, above the theme and accent color choices.
appearance_theme: Label of the light/dark choice row in the Appearance card on the Settings page.
appearance_accent: Label of the highlight-color choice row in the Appearance card on the Settings page.
appearance_follow_host: Choice button in both the 'Theme' and 'Accent' rows: use whatever the host's desktop uses. The current value may follow after a middle dot.
appearance_following: Follows 'Follow host' and a middle dot. source: where the host reads its theme from, a short identifier such as portal or windows.
appearance_none_detected: Follows 'Follow host' and a middle dot when the host's desktop reports no theme.
appearance_light: Choice button in the 'Theme' row; also names the current mode after 'Follow host' and a middle dot.
appearance_dark: Choice button in the 'Theme' row; also names the current mode after 'Follow host' and a middle dot.
appearance_custom: Screen-reader label of the text field for a color value such as #6c5bf3.
appearance_use_custom: Button beside the color field; sets the typed color as the accent.
display_q_max_mode: Question label in a device's sheet, and its text field's screen-reader label: the largest screen mode it may get, such as 2560x1440@60.
display_q_max_mode_none: Shown after 'Follow host ·' in a device's sheet: no limit on the size of its screen.
display_q_scale: Question label in a device's sheet: the zoom factor of its screen. Options are 1×, 1.25×, 1.5×, 2×.
display_q_scale_desktop: Shown after 'Follow host ·' in a device's sheet: the desktop applies its own scale.
display_capped: Part of a device's one-line display summary (parts joined by ' · '). mode: a size cap such as 2560x1440@60.
display_q_screen: Question label in a device's sheet: its own screen, or one of the host's monitors by name (DP-1).
display_own_screen: Option in a device's sheet, and part of its one-line display summary: a screen the host makes for this device alone.
display_screen_set_by_device: Under the screen question in a device's sheet when the device picked its screen in its own app.
sessions_own_display: Fact in a session row's details on the Home page: the session runs on a virtual display of its own.
sessions_joined: Fact in a session row's details on the Home page: the session shares another session's display.
sessions_shared_path: Fact in a session row's details on the Home page. names: the other devices' names, comma-separated, whose sessions share this one's network path.
sessions_plane_web: Fact in a session row's details on the Home page: the session comes from a web browser rather than an app.
sessions_link: Fact in a session row's details on the Home page. rate: the link speed the client reported, such as 940 Mbit/s or 2.5 Gbit/s.
sessions_link_wake: Fact in a session row's details. 'Frame heads' are the first packets of each video frame, which this client tends to lose.
sessions_link_lost: Fact in a session row's details. head, mid, tail: counts of packets lost in the first, middle and last part of video frames.
sessions_muted: Badge in a session row's title on the Home page: the session's audio is muted from the console.
action_mute: Button or menu item on a Home session row; silences that session's audio. Swaps with 'Unmute'.
action_unmute: Button or menu item on a muted Home session row; restores its audio. Swaps with 'Mute'.
action_mute_failed: Error toast on the Home page when muting or unmuting a session fails and the host gave no reason.
sessions_player: Label of a choice in a session row's overflow menu: which controller slot (player number) that device's gamepad takes.
sessions_player_auto: Option of the 'Player' choice: the host assigns the controller slot itself.
sessions_player_n: Badge with a gamepad icon in a session row's title, and an option of the 'Player' choice. n: slot number from 1 to 4.
action_player_failed: Error toast on the Home page when assigning a session's controller to a player number fails. 'Place' means put it in a slot.
nav_controllers: Tab on the Diagnostics page that shows the game controllers as the host receives them. Short, sits in a tab bar.
controllers_intro: Line at the top of the Controllers tab: the page shows the host's copy of the controller input, not the client's.
controllers_no_session: Empty state on the Controllers tab when no session is streaming.
controllers_no_pads: Empty state on the Controllers tab: a session is live, but its client hasn't sent any controller input.
controllers_stream_failed: Red error on the Controllers tab when the live controller feed from the host breaks.
controllers_pad: Title of a controller card on the Controllers tab. n: the controller's number.
controllers_client: Label in a controller card; the value is the name of the streaming device that owns the controller.
controllers_slot: Label in a controller card; the value is the player slot number the host gave the controller.
controllers_declared: Label in a controller card; the value is the controller type the client said it has, shown only when it differs from the one the host uses.
controllers_last_event: Label in a controller card; the value is the age of the last input, such as '240 ms ago'.
controllers_ms_ago: Age of a controller's last input, ticking live. ms: whole milliseconds.
controllers_log: Card title of the live list of controller events the host receives on the Controllers tab.
controllers_log_empty: Empty state inside the 'Event log' card. The pad is the game controller.
controllers_pause: Button in the 'Event log' header; freezes the list so it can be read.
controllers_resume: Button in the 'Event log' header while paused; lets the list move again.
controllers_copy: Button in the 'Event log' header; copies the log to the clipboard for a bug report.
controllers_copied: The same button as 'Copy', for a moment after the copy worked.
host_settings_intro: Line under the Host page's title, followed by a documentation link.
host_settings_search: Placeholder and aria-label of the search field on the Host page; it filters the settings.
host_settings_sections: aria-label (screen-reader only) of the tab strip of setting groups on the Host page.
host_settings_advanced: Checkbox label at the top of the Host page; shows the rarely needed settings.
host_settings_advanced_badge: Small badge beside the name of an advanced setting on the Host page.
host_settings_no_match: Empty state of the Host page's search. query: the text the user typed.
host_settings_locked_env: Status under a setting an environment variable fixes. name: the variable's name, such as PF_ENCODER. host.env is a file name.
host_settings_locked_flag: Status under a setting a command-line flag fixes. name: the flag, such as --native.
host_settings_applies_restart: Status under a setting that takes effect only after the host restarts.
host_settings_restart_pending: Status under a changed setting that still waits for the restart.
host_settings_reset: Tooltip of the icon button that restores a setting's default; its aria-label is this text plus the setting's name.
host_settings_save_failed: Toast and dialog error after saving a host setting failed.
host_settings_confirm_title: Title of the password dialog for changing a sensitive host setting. name: the setting's name.
host_settings_confirm_body: Body of that password dialog; the setting decides who can reach this host.
host_settings_add: Button next to the text field of a list setting; adds the typed entry.
host_settings_playing_now: Lead-in before buttons that add apps currently playing sound, in the 'Voice chat apps' setting.
settings_group_streaming: Tab on the Host page and card heading in search results: how clients connect and stream (GameStream, browser, clipboard, host name).
settings_group_video: Tab on the Host page and card heading in search results: video encoder, HDR and screen capture.
settings_group_audio: Tab on the Host page and card heading in search results: where and how audio plays, voice chat.
settings_group_input: Tab on the Host page and card heading in search results: controllers and pen input.
settings_group_network: Tab on the Host page and card heading in search results: discovery on the local network and the disconnect timeout.
settings_group_game_mode: Tab on the Host page and card heading in search results: Game Mode, the console-style gamescope session on Linux (SteamOS, Bazzite).
settings_group_session: Tab on the Host page and card heading in search results: how a streaming session and its game end or are kept after a disconnect.
settings_group_seats: Tab on the Host page and card heading in search results: defaults shared by every seat. A seat is a separate player session on this host with its own account.
settings_group_system: Tab on the Host page and card heading in search results: update checks and the tray icon.
setting_gamestream: Setting label, Streaming tab; Off/On buttons. GameStream is the protocol Moonlight clients speak; a product term.
setting_gamestream_hint: Under 'GameStream'. Moonlight is a third-party streaming client app; keep the name.
setting_webtransport: Setting label, Streaming tab; Off/On buttons. Lets the web client, Punktfunk running in a browser, connect to this host.
setting_webtransport_hint: Under 'Browser streaming'. The web client is Punktfunk's client that runs in a web browser.
setting_clipboard: Setting label, Streaming tab; buttons 'Off', 'Text', 'Text and files'. Copy and paste between a device and this host.
setting_clipboard_hint: Under 'Shared clipboard'. 'It' is the sharing; every client device has its own switch for it.
setting_clipboard_text: Button of 'Shared clipboard', beside 'Off': only copied text is shared. Short.
setting_clipboard_files: Button of 'Shared clipboard': copied files are shared as well as text. Short.
setting_host_name: Setting label, Streaming tab; text field. The name clients show for this host (the computer that streams).
setting_host_name_hint: Under 'Host name'. Blank falls back to the computer's own network name.
setting_ten_bit: Setting label, Video tab; Off/On buttons. 10-bit is the video color depth; HDR is high dynamic range.
setting_ten_bit_hint: Under '10-bit and HDR'. 'Off' is that setting's Off button; 8-bit is the standard color depth.
setting_sdr10_widen: Setting label, Video tab (advanced); Off/On buttons. SDR is standard, non-HDR dynamic range.
setting_sdr10_widen_hint: Under 'Allow 10-bit SDR'. 'Widens' converts the desktop from 8-bit to 10-bit color; a gradient is a smooth color ramp.
setting_chroma_444: Setting label, Video tab; Off/On buttons. 4:4:4 is the chroma subsampling format; keep as written.
setting_chroma_444_hint: Under 'Full color 4:4:4'. The device is the client; the GPU is the host's graphics card.
setting_max_fps: Setting label, Video tab (Linux hosts); number field followed by the unit 'fps'.
setting_max_fps_hint: Under 'Game frame limit'. 'The stream' is the video sent to the device. 0 is the value typed in the field.
setting_vdisplay_hz_mult: Setting label, Video tab (advanced); number field followed by '×'. A multiple of the stream's refresh rate.
setting_vdisplay_hz_mult_hint: Under 'Display refresh multiple'. A virtual display is a screen the host creates for the stream. 0 and 1 are values typed in the field.
setting_vdisplay_resolutions: Setting label, Video tab (Windows hosts, advanced); a list whose entries the person adds one at a time.
setting_vdisplay_resolutions_hint: Under 'Extra resolutions'. Keep the example 2560x1440 as written. The stream is the video sent to the device.
setting_audio_output_mode: Setting label, Audio tab; three buttons. Which speakers play the game's sound.
setting_audio_output_mode_client_only: Button of 'Where audio plays': sound plays only on the connected device, not on the host. 'Device' is the client.
setting_audio_output_mode_host_and_clien: Button of 'Where audio plays': sound plays on the connected device and on the host's speakers.
setting_audio_output_mode_follow_default: Button of 'Where audio plays': the host keeps using its own audio output; Punktfunk changes nothing.
setting_audio_voice_chat: Setting label, Audio tab; buttons 'In the stream', 'On the host'. Where the sound of voice chat apps such as Discord goes.
setting_audio_voice_chat_hint: Under 'Voice chat'. 'On the host' quotes that button; 'friends' are the other people in the voice call.
setting_audio_voice_chat_stream: Button of 'Voice chat': voice chat sound travels in the stream to the device, with the game's audio.
setting_audio_voice_chat_host: Button of 'Voice chat': voice chat sound plays on the host itself and stays out of the stream.
setting_audio_voice_apps: Setting label, Audio tab; a list of app names the person adds, whose sound counts as voice chat.
setting_audio_voice_apps_hint: Under 'Voice chat apps'. The built-in list is the voice chat apps Punktfunk already recognizes.
host_settings_restart_banner: Banner on the Host page when changes need a restart. names: comma-separated names of the waiting settings.
host_settings_restarting: Banner on the Host page while Punktfunk restarts.
host_settings_restarted: Toast when the host is back after a restart and all settings apply.
host_settings_restart_slow: Error toast when the host has not answered again after a restart.
diag_restart_pending_title: Health check name, bold in its row. Settings were changed that only take effect after the host restarts.
host_settings_auto: Option in settings where the host picks (encoder, cursor mode and others); shown beside On and Off in some.
setting_gamestream_encrypt: Setting label, Streaming tab (advanced); buttons 'Offer', 'Video only', 'Off', 'Require'. Encryption of Moonlight streams.
setting_gamestream_encrypt_hint: Under 'GameStream encryption'. Moonlight clients are third-party apps; keep the name.
setting_gamestream_encrypt_supported: Button of 'GameStream encryption': the host offers encryption and the client decides. A choice, not an action; short.
setting_gamestream_encrypt_video: Button of 'GameStream encryption': only the video is encrypted. Short.
setting_gamestream_encrypt_required: Button of 'GameStream encryption': the host refuses clients that don't encrypt. A choice, not an action; short.
setting_gamestream_adapt: Setting label, Streaming tab (advanced); Off/On buttons. Applies to Moonlight clients only.
setting_gamestream_adapt_hint: Under 'Adaptive bitrate'. Bitrate: video data per second. Error correction: extra data that repairs lost packets. Loss: lost packets.
setting_chacha20: Setting label, Streaming tab (advanced); Off/On buttons. ChaCha20 is an encryption algorithm; keep the name.
setting_chacha20_hint: Under 'ChaCha20 cipher'. AES hardware is a processor's built-in encryption speed-up.
setting_webtransport_origins: Setting label, Streaming tab (advanced); a list of web addresses the person adds. An origin looks like https://example.com.
setting_webtransport_origins_hint: Under 'Browser origins'. Pages are web pages running the web client. 'Empty' means the list has no entries.
setting_encoder: Setting label, Video tab; dropdown with 'Auto' and the encoder names. An encoder compresses the video.
setting_encoder_hint: Under 'Encoder'. 'Auto' is the dropdown's Auto choice.
setting_encoder_nvenc: Choice in the 'Encoder' dropdown: NVIDIA's hardware video encoder. Product name; keep.
setting_encoder_vaapi: Choice in the 'Encoder' dropdown: VA-API, the Linux interface for hardware video encoding. Name; keep.
setting_encoder_vulkan: Choice in the 'Encoder' dropdown: encoding through the Vulkan graphics API. Name; keep.
setting_encoder_pyrowave: Choice in the 'Encoder' dropdown: PyroWave, a video codec for wired links. Product name; keep.
setting_encoder_software: Choice in the 'Encoder' dropdown: encoding on the processor, not the GPU. A common word, not a product.
setting_encoder_amf: Choice in the 'Encoder' dropdown: AMD's hardware video encoder. Name; keep.
setting_encoder_qsv: Choice in the 'Encoder' dropdown: Intel's hardware video encoder. Product name.
setting_encoder_mf: Choice in the 'Encoder' dropdown: the Windows Media Foundation encoder. Product name.
setting_portal_cursor_mode: Setting label, Video tab (Linux, advanced); buttons 'Auto', 'In the picture', 'Separate', 'Hidden'. How the mouse pointer is captured.
setting_portal_cursor_mode_hint: Under 'Cursor capture'. The desktop portal is the Linux service that shares the screen with apps.
setting_portal_cursor_mode_embedded: Button of 'Cursor capture': the pointer is drawn into the video frames. Short.
setting_portal_cursor_mode_metadata: Button of 'Cursor capture': the pointer is sent apart from the video and drawn by the device. Short.
setting_portal_cursor_mode_hidden: Button of 'Cursor capture': the pointer is not captured. Short.
setting_vulkan_encode: Setting label, Video tab (Linux, advanced); Off/On buttons. Whether video is encoded through Vulkan.
setting_vulkan_encode_hint: Under 'Vulkan encoding'. 'Off' is that setting's Off button. VA-API is the Linux hardware video encoding interface.
setting_direct_capture: Setting label, Video tab (Linux, advanced); Off/On buttons. Screen capture without the desktop portal.
setting_direct_capture_hint: Under 'Direct capture'. The compositor is the Linux display server; the desktop portal is the service that shares the screen.
setting_lazy_capture: Setting label, Video tab (Linux, advanced); Off/On buttons. Capture happens when a frame is wanted, not continuously.
setting_lazy_capture_hint: Under 'On-demand capture'. A compositor is the Linux display server.
setting_kwin_paced: Setting label, Video tab (Linux, advanced); Off/On buttons. KWin is KDE's window manager; keep the name.
setting_kwin_paced_hint: Under 'KWin capture pacing'. 'It' is that setting; the pointer is the mouse pointer.
setting_pyrowave_bpp: Setting label, Video tab; number field followed by 'bits/pixel'. Picture quality of PyroWave streams.
setting_pyrowave_bpp_hint: Under 'PyroWave quality'. 1.6 is a value in bits per pixel; 'lower' is a smaller number.
setting_pyrowave_max_mbps: Setting label, Video tab (advanced); number field followed by the unit 'Mbps'. Ceiling for PyroWave stream bitrate.
setting_pyrowave_max_mbps_hint: Under 'PyroWave bitrate cap'. 0 is the value typed in the field.
setting_instant_replay_pause: Setting label, Video tab (Windows hosts); buttons 'Auto', 'On', 'Off'. Instant Replay is NVIDIA's background recording feature.
setting_instant_replay_pause_hint: Under 'Pause Instant Replay'. 'Auto' is that setting's Auto button; 'falls behind' means frames are late.
setting_audio_quality: Setting label, Audio tab; buttons 'Low', 'Standard', 'High'. Quality of the compressed audio stream.
setting_audio_quality_low: Button of 'Audio quality': lowest quality, least data. Short.
setting_audio_quality_standard: Button of 'Audio quality': the middle level. Short.
setting_audio_quality_high: Button of 'Audio quality': highest quality, most data. Short.
setting_audio_hires: Setting label, Audio tab; Off/On buttons. Audio sent without lossy compression.
setting_audio_hires_hint: Under 'Lossless audio'. Devices are the clients; uncompressed audio uses more bandwidth.
setting_pad_audio: Setting label, Audio tab (Linux, Windows); Off/On buttons. The small speaker built into some controllers, such as the DualSense.
setting_pad_audio_hint: Under 'Controller speaker'. Haptics are the controller's vibration feedback.
setting_audio_redundancy: Setting label, Audio tab (advanced); buttons 'Auto', 'On', 'Off'. Sending audio packets twice so losses don't cause dropouts.
setting_audio_redundancy_hint: Under 'Audio redundancy'. A lossy link is a network that drops packets; 'Auto' is that setting's Auto button.
setting_gamepad: Setting label, Input tab (Linux, Windows); dropdown with 'Auto' and controller models. The controller type the host shows games.
setting_gamepad_hint: Under 'Default gamepad'. A device is a client; 'pick one' means it asks for a controller type itself.
setting_gamepad_xbox360: Choice in the 'Default gamepad' dropdown: Microsoft's Xbox 360 controller. Product name; keep.
setting_gamepad_xboxone: Choice in the 'Default gamepad' dropdown: Microsoft's Xbox One controller. Product name; keep.
setting_gamepad_xboxelite: Choice in the 'Default gamepad' dropdown: Microsoft's Xbox Elite controller. Product name; keep.
setting_gamepad_dualsense: Choice in the 'Default gamepad' dropdown: Sony's PlayStation 5 controller. Product name; keep.
setting_gamepad_dualsenseedge: Choice in the 'Default gamepad' dropdown: Sony's DualSense Edge controller for PlayStation 5. Product name; keep.
setting_gamepad_dualshock4: Choice in the 'Default gamepad' dropdown: Sony's PlayStation 4 controller. Product name; keep.
setting_gamepad_steamdeck: Choice in the 'Default gamepad' dropdown: the Steam Deck's built-in controls. Product name; keep.
setting_gamepad_steamcontroller: Choice in the 'Default gamepad' dropdown: Valve's original Steam Controller. Product name; keep.
setting_gamepad_steamcontroller2: Choice in the 'Default gamepad' dropdown: Valve's second-generation Steam Controller. Product name; keep.
setting_gamepad_switchpro: Choice in the 'Default gamepad' dropdown: Nintendo's Switch Pro Controller. Product name; keep.
setting_gamepad_steamcontroller2puck: Choice in the 'Default gamepad' dropdown: the Steam Controller 2 used through its wireless puck receiver. Product name; keep.
setting_gamepad_joyconpair: Choice in the 'Default gamepad' dropdown: two Nintendo Joy-Con controllers working as one gamepad. Product name; keep.
setting_gamepad_switch2pro: Choice in the 'Default gamepad' dropdown: Nintendo's Switch 2 Pro Controller. Product name; keep.
setting_gamepad_switch2gamecube: Choice in the 'Default gamepad' dropdown: Nintendo's GameCube-style controller for Switch 2. Product name; keep.
setting_gamepad_8bitdoultimate2: Choice in the 'Default gamepad' dropdown: 8BitDo's Ultimate 2 controller. Product name; keep.
setting_gamepad_8bitdopro2: Choice in the 'Default gamepad' dropdown: 8BitDo's Pro 2 controller. Product name; keep.
setting_gamepad_8bitdopro3: Choice in the 'Default gamepad' dropdown: 8BitDo's Pro 3 controller. Product name; keep.
setting_gamepad_horipadsteam: Choice in the 'Default gamepad' dropdown: HORI's HORIPAD for Steam controller. Product name; keep.
setting_pen: Setting label, Input tab (Linux, Windows); Off/On buttons. Stylus input from a tablet or pen display.
setting_pen_hint: Under 'Pen input'. Tablets are the client devices that have a stylus.
setting_steam_gadget: Setting label, Input tab (Linux, advanced); buttons 'Auto', 'On', 'Off'. A USB gadget is a Linux device acting as a USB device.
setting_steam_gadget_hint: Under 'Steam USB gadget'. SteamOS is Valve's Linux system; 'Auto' is that setting's Auto button.
setting_dualsense_usbip: Setting label, Input tab (Linux, advanced); Off/On buttons. USB/IP is a protocol that carries USB over a network; keep as written.
setting_dualsense_usbip_hint: Under 'DualSense over USB/IP'. A real sound card is an actual audio device the system sees for the controller's speaker.
setting_gamescope_hdr: Setting label, Game Mode tab (Linux); Off/On buttons. Game Mode is the console-style gamescope session; HDR is high dynamic range.
setting_gamescope_hdr_hint: Under 'Game Mode HDR'. 'Off' is that setting's Off button; SDR is standard, non-HDR range.
setting_gamescope_managed: Setting label, Game Mode tab (Linux, advanced); Off/On buttons. Managed means Punktfunk launches and controls the Game Mode session.
setting_gamescope_managed_hint: Under 'Force managed mode'. Game Mode is the console-style gamescope session; the device is the client.
setting_gamescope_vrr: Setting label, Game Mode tab (Linux, advanced); Off/On buttons. Variable refresh rate, as in G-Sync or FreeSync.
setting_gamescope_vrr_hint: Under 'Adaptive sync'. Game Mode is the console-style gamescope session; 'draw a frame' means show a new picture.
setting_gamescope_sdr_nits: Setting label, Game Mode tab (Linux, advanced); number field followed by the unit 'nits' (brightness).
setting_gamescope_sdr_nits_hint: Under 'SDR brightness'. SDR is standard dynamic range; HDR is high dynamic range.
setting_gamescope_refresh_rates: Setting label, Game Mode tab (Linux, advanced); a list of refresh rates the person adds.
setting_gamescope_refresh_rates_hint: Under 'Extra refresh rates'. Hz is the unit; a device is a client.
setting_gamescope_splash: Setting label, Game Mode tab (Linux, advanced); Off/On buttons. A splash is an image shown while the session starts.
setting_gamescope_splash_hint: Under 'Startup splash'. A splash is an image shown while the session starts.
setting_gamescope_isolate: Setting label, Game Mode tab (Linux, advanced); Off/On buttons. Isolation keeps sessions apart from one another.
setting_gamescope_isolate_hint: Under 'Per-session isolation'. Input is keyboard, mouse and controllers.
setting_gamescope_grab_cursor: Setting label, Game Mode tab (Linux, advanced); Off/On buttons. Whether the mouse pointer is confined to the game.
setting_gamescope_grab_cursor_hint: Under 'Grab the cursor'. Menus that expect a free pointer stop working.
setting_gamescope_bind: Setting label, Game Mode tab (Linux, advanced); buttons 'Auto', 'On', 'Off'. Bind means to mount over: Punktfunk's own gamescope build replaces the system one.
setting_gamescope_bind_hint: Under 'Bind patched gamescope'. Game Mode is the console-style gamescope session; keep the name gamescope.
setting_session_watch: Setting label, Game Mode tab (Linux, advanced); buttons 'Auto', 'On', 'Off'. Whether a stream follows the host switching modes.
setting_session_watch_hint: Under 'Follow mode switches'. Game Mode is the console-style gamescope session; the desktop is the normal Linux desktop.
setting_mdns: Setting label, Network tab (advanced); Off/On buttons. mDNS is the protocol that lets devices find this host without typing an address.
setting_mdns_hint: Under 'Local discovery'. 'Off' is that setting's Off button; 'adding it by address' is typing the host's IP in a client.
setting_idle_timeout_ms: Setting label, Network tab (advanced); number field followed by the unit 'ms'. Time before a silent connection is dropped.
setting_idle_timeout_ms_hint: Under 'Disconnect timeout'. A silent device is a client that stopped sending data; the host lets go of its session.
setting_update_check: Setting label, System tab; Off/On buttons. Whether the console looks for new Punktfunk versions.
setting_update_check_hint: Under 'Check for updates'. The update server is where new Punktfunk versions are published.
setting_update_apply: Setting label, System tab (advanced); Off/On buttons. The console is the web console that manages this host.
setting_update_apply_hint: Under 'Console updates'. 'Off' is that setting's Off button; the console is the web console; 'them' means updates.
setting_steam_prewarm: Setting label, Seats tab; number field followed by 'seats'. Warm means already started and ready.
setting_steam_prewarm_hint: Under 'Seats kept warm'. A seat is a separate player session on this host; the most recent players are the last people who played.
setting_seat_idle_stop: Setting label, Seats tab; a lead-in to the number field and the unit 'min' that follow it.
setting_seat_idle_stop_hint: Under 'Stop an idle seat after'. A seat is a separate player session; 0 is the value typed in the field.
setting_seat_end_on_game_exit: Setting label, Seats tab; Off/On buttons. A seat is a separate player session on this host.
setting_seat_end_on_game_exit_hint: Under 'End a seat's stream when its game exits'. 'Off' is that setting's Off button.
setting_seat_max_mode: Setting label, Seats tab; text field. A mode is resolution plus refresh rate.
setting_seat_max_mode_hint: Under 'Highest mode per seat'. Keep 2560x1440@120 as written; a device's own cap is a limit the device sets itself.
setting_seat_library_writable: Setting label, Seats tab (Linux); Off/On buttons. Whether seats may change the owner's Steam game libraries.
setting_seat_library_writable_hint: Under 'Seats update your games'. 'Off:' is that setting's Off button; libraries are Steam game libraries.
setting_seat_background_input: Setting label, Seats tab (Windows); Off/On buttons. Each player's controller keeps working while another player's window is in front.
setting_seat_background_input_hint: Under 'Players keep their controllers'. 'This PC' is the host computer; switches apps means another window comes to the front.
setting_tray_autostart: Setting label, System tab (Linux, Windows); Off/On buttons. The tray icon is Punktfunk's status icon.
setting_tray_autostart_hint: Under 'Tray autostart'. The status icon sits in the system tray beside the clock; sign-in means the person logging in to the computer.
library_search_placeholder: Placeholder and screen-reader label of the search box above the games.
library_platform_all: Option of the platform filter above the games: no filtering.
library_platform_label: Screen-reader label of the platform filter dropdown above the games.
library_platform_option: Option of the platform filter. platform: a system name such as PS2; count: number of games.
library_view_grid: Icon-button tooltip and screen-reader label: shows the games as cover tiles.
library_view_rows: Icon-button tooltip and screen-reader label: shows the games as a list.
library_count: Plural. Count line above the games. count: number of games matching.
library_count_shown: Plural. Count line above the games while only part is loaded. shown: loaded so far; count: all matching.
library_load_more: Button below the games; loads the next page.
library_no_matches: Library page empty state when the search or filters match no game.
library_tab_games: Tab on the Library page: the games.
library_tab_sources: Tab on the Library page: where games come from. A badge counts pending folder requests.
library_open_sources: Button in the Library empty state; switches to the Sources tab.
library_filter_source: Chip above the games while narrowed to one source. source: the source's name. Pressing it clears the filter.
library_filter_clear: Tooltip on the chip 'Only {source}'; pressing it shows all sources again.
nav_profiles: Sidebar and phone-bar entry for the page where profiles are managed: the people who play on this host, each with their own desktop.
nav_profiles_hint: Second line under 'Profiles' in the phone's More menu; says what the page is for. One line, may be cut off.
profiles_title: Title of the Profiles page. A profile is one person's identity on this host: a name, picture and color, and where it plays.
profiles_add: Button in the Profiles page header, and title and submit button of the Add profile dialog.
profiles_owner: Badge on the profile that belongs to the host's owner, the PC's own user.
profiles_plays_owner: Part of a profile row's gray info line, joined with ' · ', for the owner's profile: it plays on the PC's own desktop.
profiles_plays_shared: Part of a profile row's gray info line, joined with ' · '. owner: the owner profile's name.
profiles_state_ready: Badge on a profile with a desktop of its own, and status on the Displays page's 'Other desktops' rows: running and free.
profiles_state_starting: Same badge and status as 'Ready': the desktop is starting up.
profiles_state_stopped: Same badge and status as 'Ready': the desktop is switched off.
profiles_state_occupied: Badge on a profile row: a device is streaming that profile's desktop right now.
profiles_state_unavailable: Red badge on a profile row, and status on 'Other desktops': the desktop can't be used at the moment.
profiles_occupied_by: Part of a profile row's info line and a status on 'Other desktops'. device: name of the device streaming it.
profiles_home_desktop: Part of a profile row's info line: when this profile connects, the stream opens on the plain desktop.
profiles_home_bigpicture: Part of a profile row's info line: the stream opens in Steam's Big Picture mode. Big Picture is a Steam term.
profiles_last_used: Part of a profile row's info line. when: a formatted date and time of the last stream.
profiles_never_used: Part of a profile row's info line: nobody has streamed with this profile yet.
profiles_name: Label of the name field in the Add profile dialog and in the rename prompt.
profiles_color: Legend of the color swatches in the Add profile dialog. The color tints the profile's avatar.
profiles_color_custom: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the last, rainbow swatch that opens the system color picker.
profiles_picture_set: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the round avatar in Add profile and of the image button on a profile row; opens a file picker.
profiles_picture_remove: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the remove-picture button on a profile row; also a small text button under the avatar in Add profile.
profiles_picture_optional: Small caption under the avatar in the Add profile dialog while no picture is chosen; clicking the avatar adds one.
profiles_picture_failed: Error toast when saving or removing a profile's picture fails. PNG and JPEG are file types; 1 MB is the size limit.
profiles_rename_title: Title of the prompt opened by the pencil button on a profile row.
profiles_rename_failed: Error toast when renaming a profile fails.
profiles_remove: Verb. Tooltip and screen-reader label of the trash button on a profile row, and the red submit button of the remove dialog.
profiles_remove_title: Title of the remove-profile dialog. name: the profile's name.
profiles_remove_body: First sentence in the remove dialog's body; another sentence about the account may follow. name: the profile's name.
profiles_remove_erase: Checkbox in the remove dialog, shown when the profile has its own Steam on this host. name: the profile's name.
profiles_remove_failed: Error line in the remove dialog when removing fails and the host gave no reason.
profiles_plays_question: Group heading above the choice cards in the Add profile dialog; the cards are its answers.
profiles_outcome_shared: Choice card in Add profile, under 'Where this profile plays'. owner: the owner profile's name. Also the info line of such a profile.
profiles_outcome_shared_hint: Description on the 'Shares {owner}'s desktop' choice card.
profiles_outcome_desktop: Choice card in Add profile: a desktop of its own for the profile (a seat). Also in a profile row's info line.
profiles_outcome_needs_seats: Description on the disabled 'Own desktop' card when the host can't run seats at all.
profiles_add_failed: Error toast when adding a profile fails and the host gave no reason.
profiles_outcome_desktop_hint: Description on the 'Own desktop' choice card on a Windows host with seats on.
profiles_outcome_seats_off: Description on the disabled 'Own desktop' card on Windows while seats are off; the page's Seats button turns them on.
profiles_outcome_needs_server: Description on the disabled 'Own desktop' card on a Windows edition that can't run seats. Windows Server is a Microsoft product.
profiles_outcome_account: Choice card in Add profile, Windows: the profile uses an existing Windows account and players take turns on the PC. Also in a row's info line.
profiles_outcome_account_hint: Description on the 'Own account (take turns)' choice card.
profiles_outcome_account_none: Description on the disabled 'Own account (take turns)' card when the PC has no free Windows account.
profiles_account_which: Label of the Windows account dropdown in the Add profile dialog.
profiles_account_pick: Placeholder of the Windows account dropdown, before one is chosen.
profiles_account_turns: Help under the account dropdown when 'Own account (take turns)' is chosen.
profiles_remove_windows: Sentence appended to the remove dialog's body after 'Sessions playing as {name} end now.', Windows. name: the profile's name.
profiles_seat_starting: Info line of a profile row (also on the Home page) while its own desktop starts and the host gives no detail.
profiles_seat_start: Button on a profile row whose own desktop is stopped; starts it.
profiles_seat_stop: Button on a profile row, and on the Home page for a starting desktop; shuts the profile's own desktop down.
profiles_seat_end: Button on a profile row and on the Home page while someone streams that desktop; ends their session, the desktop keeps running.
profiles_seat_failed: Error toast when starting, stopping or ending a profile's desktop fails and the host gave no reason.
profiles_seats: Button in the Windows Profiles page header, and title of the dialog that turns seats on or off. A seat is a desktop of its own for one profile.
profiles_seats_on: Checkbox in the Seats dialog; turns seats on for the whole PC.
profiles_seats_confirm_title: Title of the console-password dialog shown when a setting in the Seats dialog changes.
profiles_seats_confirm_body: Body of that password dialog. The console password is the one for signing in to this web console.
profiles_seats_rdp: Checkbox in the Seats dialog. Remote Desktop is Microsoft's RDP; 'from the network' means from other computers.
profiles_seats_rdp_hint: Under the Remote Desktop checkbox. 'Off' and 'on' refer to that checkbox.
profiles_seats_failed: Error line in the Seats password dialog when the change fails and the host gave no reason.
profiles_seats_healthy: Line under the profile cards on a seat host when the Doctor found nothing wrong; beside the 'Doctor' button.
